198	# ==========================================================================
199	# TASK #11 — the d=2048 roofline 3-point comparison (compile.py vs nvcc).
200	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
201	# The full-_ops path above builds at the PRODUCTION toy d=128 config (the only
202	# config the production cell + fp64 gate run at). "See the real difference"
203	# wants the comparison at the d=2048 ROOFLINE scale where the kernel actually
204	# stresses the GEMM pipe — but only the coexisting BENCH translation unit
205	# (csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc.cu, -DSG_DEC_BENCH_LAYOUT=1 →
206	# the _DEC_BENCH_D=2048 layout branch) compiles at d=2048. So the d=2048 leg
207	# builds THAT single TU three ways and times its tc_train_step (the SAME path
208	# tuning/decoder_bench.py uses), differing ONLY in (1) the nvcc flag set and
209	# (2) the dW split-K macro:
210	#
211	#   A  regular nvcc        : VANILLA flags (-O3 [+--use_fast_math] -arch=sm_90a
212	#                            + only the structural -D needed to compile), NO
213	#                            compile.py ptxas tuning;            split-K = 4.
214	#   B  compile.py default  : compile.py's AUGMENTED flags (NVCC_DEVICE_BASE +
215	#                            the CUDA-version-gated ptxas tuning ladder +
216	#                            grokking's --use_fast_math -DNDEBUG, exactly the
217	#                            setup.py production line);          split-K = 4.
218	#   C  compile.py tuned    : same augmented flags + the TUNED knob (the
219	#                            in-source default);                 split-K = 2.
220	#
221	# A→B isolates the compilation-pipeline benefit (the ptxas-tuning flags);
222	# B→C isolates the autotuner's knob benefit; A→C is the total. fast-math is
223	# held IDENTICAL across A/B/C (production B uses it — see setup.py:643), so
224	# A→B is purely the ptxas-tuning flags, not a numerics confound.
225	# ==========================================================================
226	
227	# Structural -D the bench TU needs to compile at d=2048 (mirrors
228	# tuning/decoder_bench.build_variant: the d!=128 bench branch). NOT opt flags.
229	_BENCH_STRUCTURAL = [
230	    "-DSG_TUNED_GEMM_IMPL=1",     # select the wgmma cell driver
231	    "-DSG_DEC_BENCH_LAYOUT=1",    # → the _DEC_BENCH_D=2048 layout branch
232	    "-DSG_DEC_SCALAR_MEGAKERNEL=0",  # gate off the legacy scalar megakernel
233	                                     # (its smem grows with d and ptxas
234	                                     # hard-stops at d>=768; never driven here)
235	]
236	_BENCH_GENCODE = ["-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=sm_90a",
237	                  "-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=compute_90a"]
238	_BENCH_TU = os.path.join(ROOT, "csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc.cu")
239	
240	
241	def _vanilla_bench_nvcc(fast_math: bool) -> list:
242	    """Variant A — what a competent dev would hand-write: -O3 [+--use_fast_math]
243	    -arch=sm_90a + the structural defines. Explicitly NONE of compile.py's
244	    ptxas micro-tuning (no --register-usage-level / --def-load-cache /
245	    --def-store-cache / --extra-device-vectorization / -Xfatbin -compress-all /
246	    --opt-level=3 / -v)."""
247	    flags = ["-O3", "-std=c++17", "--expt-relaxed-constexpr"]
248	    if fast_math:
249	        flags.append("--use_fast_math")
250	    return flags + _BENCH_GENCODE + _BENCH_STRUCTURAL
251	
252	
253	def _augmented_bench_nvcc() -> list:
254	    """Variants B/C — the EXACT production compile.py flag line for this single
255	    TU on this toolchain: NVCC_DEVICE_BASE + the CUDA-version-gated ptxas
256	    tuning ladder (probed live) + grokking's project flags (--use_fast_math
257	    -DNDEBUG -lineinfo), exactly as setup.py composes it. fast-math ON to match
258	    A (and production)."""
259	    from grokking_optimizers.compile import (NVCC_DEVICE_BASE,
260	                                             _newer_compiler_flags)
261	    base = list(NVCC_DEVICE_BASE)
262	    # The CUDA-version-gated additions (register-usage-level=10 on 12.3+,
263	    # def-load-cache=ca, def-store-cache=wb, --threads, --diag-suppress, …) —
264	    # the SAME ladder the production/autotuner device compile uses.
265	    # _newer_compiler_flags returns (extra_host, extra_device); take device.
266	    try:
267	        _host, gated = _newer_compiler_flags("sm_90")
268	    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - never block the comparison
269	        sys.stderr.write(f"[nvcc-baseline] WARN: _newer_compiler_flags failed "
270	                         f"({exc}); proceeding with NVCC_DEVICE_BASE only\n")
271	        gated = []
272	    # grokking project flags (setup.py:643) + bench structural + gencode.
273	    return (base + list(gated) + ["--use_fast_math", "-DNDEBUG", "-lineinfo"]
274	            + _BENCH_GENCODE + _BENCH_STRUCTURAL)
275	
276	
277	def _build_bench_variant(label: str, nvcc_flags: list, splitk: int,
278	                         fast_math: bool, verbose: bool):
279	    """JIT-build the d=2048 decoder bench TU with a fully-specified nvcc flag
280	    set + a dW split-K override. Distinct module name + build dir so the three
281	    variants coexist (and never touch the production _ops.so)."""
282	    from torch.utils.cpp_extension import load as _load
283	    flags = list(nvcc_flags) + [f"-DSG_TUNED_DEC_DW_SPLITK={splitk}"]
284	    name = f"mega_decoder_d2048_task11_{label}_sk{splitk}"
285	    bdir = os.path.join("/workspace", "task11_bench_build", f"{label}_sk{splitk}")
286	    os.makedirs(bdir, exist_ok=True)
287	    os.environ.setdefault("TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST", "9.0a")
288	    cxx = ["-O3", "-std=c++17"]
289	    if fast_math:
290	        cxx.append("-ffast-math")
291	    sys.stderr.write(f"[nvcc-baseline][{label}] split-K={splitk} fast_math={fast_math}\n")
292	    sys.stderr.write(f"[nvcc-baseline][{label}] nvcc flags: {' '.join(flags)}\n")
293	    mod = _load(name=name, sources=[_BENCH_TU],
294	                extra_include_paths=[ROOT],
295	                extra_cuda_cflags=flags,
296	                extra_cflags=cxx,
297	                build_directory=bdir,
298	                verbose=verbose)
299	    return mod
300	
301	
302	def _time_bench_seed(DB, mod, d: int, batch: int, seed: int,
303	                     reps: int, warmup: int, iters: int):
304	    """Median step-ms for ONE seed: inputs reseeded per-seed (params/tokens from
305	    a per-seed generator — the genuine 3-seed coverage, vs decoder_bench.measure
306	    which hardcodes seed 42). Shapes/work are identical across seeds, so this is
307	    the protocol's timing-variance probe at the d=2048 roofline (correctness +
308	    determinism are the SEPARATE fp64 gate). Mirrors roofline_bench.time_seed."""
309	    import time as _t
310	    dev = torch.device("cuda")
311	    total = int(mod.TOTAL)
312	    vocab, seq = int(mod.VOCAB), int(mod.SEQ)
313	    g = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(seed)
314	    params = (torch.randn(total, generator=g, device=dev) * 0.02).contiguous()
315	    tokens = torch.randint(0, vocab, (batch, seq), generator=g,
316	                           device=dev).to(torch.int32).contiguous()
317	    targets = torch.randint(0, vocab, (batch,), generator=g,
318	                            device=dev).to(torch.int32).contiguous()
319	    state = torch.zeros(3 * total, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
320	    lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd = 1e-3, 0.9, 0.98, 1e-8, 0.0
321	    bc1, bc2 = 1.0 - beta1, 1.0 - beta2
322	
323	    def call():
324	        return mod.tc_train_step(params, tokens, targets, state, lr, beta1,
325	                                 beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2, 1, 0)
326	
327	    for _ in range(warmup):
328	        call()
329	    torch.cuda.synchronize()
330	    walls = []
331	    for _ in range(reps):
332	        torch.cuda.synchronize()
333	        t0 = _t.perf_counter()
334	        for _ in range(iters):
335	            call()
336	        torch.cuda.synchronize()
337	        walls.append((_t.perf_counter() - t0) / iters * 1e3)
338	    return statistics.median(walls), [round(w, 4) for w in walls]
339	
340	
341	def _run_d2048_3point(args) -> int:
342	    """A/B/C build + 3-seed median step-ms + TF/s + deltas at d=2048."""
343	    import tuning.decoder_bench as DB
344	    import time as _time
345	    fast_math = not args.strict_math
346	    d, batch = 2048, args.batch
347	    assert batch % 16 == 0, "B must be divisible by 16"
348	
349	    variants = [
350	        ("A", "regular-nvcc (vanilla flags, split-K=4)",
351	         _vanilla_bench_nvcc(fast_math), 4),
352	        ("B", "compile.py-default (augmented flags, split-K=4)",
353	         _augmented_bench_nvcc(), 4),
354	        ("C", "compile.py-tuned (augmented flags, split-K=2)",
355	         _augmented_bench_nvcc(), 2),
356	    ]
357	    seeds = [int(s) for s in args.seeds.split(",") if s.strip()]
358	    results = {}
359	    for label, desc, nvcc_flags, splitk in variants:
360	        sys.stderr.write(f"\n[nvcc-baseline] ===== variant {label}: {desc} =====\n")
361	        t0 = _time.perf_counter()
362	        mod = _build_bench_variant(label, nvcc_flags, splitk, fast_math,
363	                                   args.verbose_build)
364	        build_s = _time.perf_counter() - t0
365	        assert int(mod.D) == d, f"variant {label} compiled D={int(mod.D)} != {d}"
366	        flops = DB._decoder_gemm_flops_per_step(
367	            d, batch, int(mod.LAYERS), int(mod.SEQ), int(mod.VOCAB))
368	        per_seed, per_seed_walls = {}, {}
369	        for s in seeds:
370	            med_s, walls = _time_bench_seed(DB, mod, d, batch, s, args.reps,
371	                                            args.warmup, args.iters)
372	            per_seed[s] = med_s
373	            per_seed_walls[s] = walls
374	        med = statistics.median(per_seed.values())
375	        tf_s = flops / (med / 1e3) / 1e12
376	        rec = {"variant": label, "desc": desc, "split_k": splitk,
377	               "fast_math": fast_math, "d": d, "B": batch,
378	               "total_params": int(mod.TOTAL), "build_s": round(build_s, 1),
379	               "per_seed_median_ms": {s: round(per_seed[s], 4) for s in seeds},
380	               "per_seed_walls_ms": per_seed_walls,
381	               "across_seed_median_ms": round(med, 4),
382	               "achieved_tf_s": round(tf_s, 3),
383	               "pct_roofline": round(100.0 * tf_s / 989.0, 3)}
384	        results[label] = rec
385	        sys.stdout.write("VARIANT " + json.dumps(rec) + "\n")
386	        sys.stdout.flush()
387	
388	    # Deltas (negative = faster). A→B = pipeline/flags; B→C = autotuner; A→C = total.
389	    a, b, c = (results[k]["across_seed_median_ms"] for k in "ABC")
390	    deltas = {
391	        "A_to_B_pipeline_flags_pct": round(100.0 * (b - a) / a, 3),
392	        "B_to_C_autotuner_pct": round(100.0 * (c - b) / b, 3),

"""scripts/nvcc_baseline.py — a TRUE "regular nvcc" baseline build of the _ops
extension, for the Task-#11 three-point comparison:

    A  regular nvcc        (this script)          — plain -O3 [+ --use_fast_math],
                                                     NO compile.py ptxas tuning
    B  compile.py default  (build.sh / setup.py)  — augmented flags, in-source
                                                     SG_TUNED defaults  (A→B = the
                                                     compile.py *pipeline* benefit)
    C  compile.py JIT-tuned (autotuner winner)     — B + SG_TUNED knob search
                                                     (B→C = the *autotuner* benefit)

It compiles the SAME 6 production translation units (bindings, dispatch, the 3
mega_<model>_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu, sg2_meta_tail.cu) as setup.py, but with a
VANILLA nvcc flag set: only the flags needed to *compile* (gencode, CUTLASS +
feature -D macros, NDEBUG, fPIC, --expt-relaxed-constexpr) plus the obvious
-O3 [+ --use_fast_math] a competent dev would write — and explicitly NONE of
compile.py's ptxas micro-tuning (--register-usage-level, --def-load-cache/
--def-store-cache, --extra-device-vectorization, --maxrregcount, -Xfatbin
-compress-all). So B-vs-A isolates exactly what those tuning flags buy.

The freshly-built .so is aliased as ``grokking_optimizers._ops`` (the proven
idiom from grokking_optimizers/tune_hook.py:_alias_variant_ops) so the production
dispatch + the fp64 gate run against THIS binary, then we time the cell with
CUDA events exactly like scripts/time_cell.py.

Usage:
  python scripts/nvcc_baseline.py --model decoder --opt adamw \
      --seeds 42,7,123 --warmup 10 --iters 30 --reps 5 [--strict-math]
Prints one TIMING json line per seed (median per-step wall-ms).
"""
import argparse
import glob
import importlib.util
import json
import os
import statistics
import sys

import torch
from torch.utils.cpp_extension import load as _cpp_load

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Resolve the EXACT production source set (mirrors setup.py's glob+filter).
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _owns_extension_module(path: str) -> bool:
    if not path.endswith(".cu"):
        return False
    try:
        with open(path, "r", errors="ignore") as fh:
            return "PYBIND11_MODULE(TORCH_EXTENSION_NAME" in fh.read()
    except OSError:
        return False


def _resolve_sources() -> list:
    pats = ["csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/*.cu",
            "csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/models/*.cu",
            "csrc/fused/sm_90/*.cu"]
    out = []
    for pat in pats:
        out += sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, pat)))
    common = [os.path.join(ROOT, "csrc/bindings/bindings.cpp"),
              os.path.join(ROOT, "csrc/bindings/dispatch.cpp")]
    cu = [s for s in out
          if "_overlay" not in os.path.basename(s)
          and not s.endswith("_selftest.cu")
          and not _owns_extension_module(s)]
    return common + cu


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) VANILLA flag sets (regular nvcc) — NO compile.py ptxas tuning.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Structural defines the kernels need to COMPILE (gate #ifdef branches); these
# are NOT optimization flags — dropping them would change which code compiles,
# not how fast it runs. Mirrors setup.py's cuda_define_macros + CUTLASS block.
_STRUCTURAL_DEFINES = [
    "-DWITH_CUDA", "-DWITH_CUTLASS",
    "-DCUTLASS_NVCC_ARCHS=90a", "-DCUTLASS_NVCC_ARCHS_SUPPORTED=90a",
    "-DCUDA_TMA_ENABLED=1", "-DCUDA_WGMMA_ENABLED=1",
    "-DCUDA_CLUSTER_ENABLED=1", "-DCUDA_FP8_ENABLED=1",
    "-DCUDA_FORCE_CDP1_IF_SUPPORTED", "-DNDEBUG",
]
# sm_90a ONLY (cubin + matching PTX). The megakernel emits wgmma.* PTX, which
# requires the ``a`` (architecture-specific) target — assembling it for plain
# ``compute_90`` makes ptxas reject every wgmma instruction ("not supported on
# .target 'sm_90'"). So the embedded-PTX line must also be compute_90a (mirrors
# setup.py's _supported_gencode(min_cc=90) Hopper/CUTLASS path).
_GENCODE = ["-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=sm_90a",
            "-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=compute_90a"]
_INCLUDES = [".", "csrc/bindings", "csrc",
             "third_party/cutlass/include",
             "third_party/cutlass/tools/util/include"]


def _vanilla_nvcc(fast_math: bool) -> list:
    flags = ["-O3", "-std=c++17", "--expt-relaxed-constexpr"]
    if fast_math:
        flags.append("--use_fast_math")
    return flags + _STRUCTURAL_DEFINES + _GENCODE


def _vanilla_cxx(fast_math: bool) -> list:
    flags = ["-O3", "-std=c++17", "-fPIC"]
    if fast_math:
        flags.append("-ffast-math")
    return flags + ["-DWITH_CUDA", "-DWITH_CUTLASS", "-DNDEBUG"]


def _build_vanilla(fast_math: bool):
    sources = _resolve_sources()
    # Pin the arch so torch's BuildExtension does NOT auto-detect and inject its
    # own `-gencode arch=compute_90,code=compute_90` (the non-`a` PTX target),
    # which makes ptxas reject the megakernel's wgmma.* PTX ("not supported on
    # .target 'sm_90'"). 9.0a => torch emits sm_90a/compute_90a only, matching
    # _GENCODE above and the production/bench builds. (setdefault is not enough —
    # an inherited value would leak the default; set it explicitly.)
    os.environ["TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST"] = "9.0a"
    sys.stderr.write(f"[nvcc-baseline] {len(sources)} TUs, fast_math={fast_math}, "
                     f"TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=9.0a\n")
    sys.stderr.write("[nvcc-baseline] nvcc flags: "
                     + " ".join(_vanilla_nvcc(fast_math)) + "\n")
    # name="_ops" so PYBIND11_MODULE(TORCH_EXTENSION_NAME) emits PyInit__ops,
    # matching what grokking_optimizers._ops expects.
    mod = _cpp_load(
        name="_ops",
        sources=sources,
        extra_cflags=_vanilla_cxx(fast_math),
        extra_cuda_cflags=_vanilla_nvcc(fast_math),
        extra_include_paths=[os.path.join(ROOT, p) for p in _INCLUDES],
        build_directory=_ensure_build_dir(fast_math),
        verbose=True,
    )
    return mod


def _ensure_build_dir(fast_math: bool) -> str:
    tag = "fastmath" if fast_math else "strict"
    d = os.path.join("/workspace", "nvcc_baseline_build", tag)
    os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    return d


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Alias the freshly-built .so as grokking_optimizers._ops (tune_hook idiom).
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _alias_as_ops(built_module) -> None:
    # The cpp_extension.load() return value is already the imported module
    # object; evict any stale grokking_optimizers._ops (+ submodules + dispatch
    # + optimizers that memoize the resolved ops) so the production dispatch
    # binds THIS binary, then alias it.
    for k in [k for k in list(sys.modules)
              if k == "grokking_optimizers._ops"
              or k.startswith("grokking_optimizers._ops.")
              or k == "grokking_optimizers.dispatch"]:
        del sys.modules[k]
    sys.modules["grokking_optimizers._ops"] = built_module


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4) Time the cell with CUDA events (mirrors scripts/time_cell.py).
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _time_cell(model: str, opt: str, seed: int, warmup: int, iters: int,
               reps: int) -> dict:
    os.environ["GATE_SEED"] = str(seed)
    import tests.hw.test_l3tc_tail_gate as G
    from grokking_optimizers.dispatch import fused_train_step  # noqa: F401
    g, c, m, data, dev = G._build_cell(model)
    tx, ty = data[0], data[1]
    spec = G._CELLS[f"{opt}/{model}"]
    opt_obj = spec["factory"](g, m.parameters(), c)

    def _step():
        fused_train_step(m, opt_obj, tx, ty)

    for _ in range(warmup):
        _step()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    medians = []
    for _ in range(reps):
        start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
        end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
        start.record()
        for _ in range(iters):
            _step()
        end.record()
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        medians.append(start.elapsed_time(end) / iters)
    return {"model": model, "opt": opt, "seed": seed,
            "median_ms": statistics.median(medians),
            "min_ms": min(medians),
            "walls_ms": [round(x, 4) for x in medians]}


# ==========================================================================
# TASK #11 — the d=2048 roofline 3-point comparison (compile.py vs nvcc).
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The full-_ops path above builds at the PRODUCTION toy d=128 config (the only
# config the production cell + fp64 gate run at). "See the real difference"
# wants the comparison at the d=2048 ROOFLINE scale where the kernel actually
# stresses the GEMM pipe — but only the coexisting BENCH translation unit
# (csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc.cu, -DSG_DEC_BENCH_LAYOUT=1 →
# the _DEC_BENCH_D=2048 layout branch) compiles at d=2048. So the d=2048 leg
# builds THAT single TU three ways and times its tc_train_step (the SAME path
# tuning/decoder_bench.py uses), differing ONLY in (1) the nvcc flag set and
# (2) the dW split-K macro:
#
#   A  regular nvcc        : VANILLA flags (-O3 [+--use_fast_math] -arch=sm_90a
#                            + only the structural -D needed to compile), NO
#                            compile.py ptxas tuning;            split-K = 4.
#   B  compile.py default  : compile.py's AUGMENTED flags (NVCC_DEVICE_BASE +
#                            the CUDA-version-gated ptxas tuning ladder +
#                            grokking's --use_fast_math -DNDEBUG, exactly the
#                            setup.py production line);          split-K = 4.
#   C  compile.py tuned    : same augmented flags + the TUNED knob (the
#                            in-source default);                 split-K = 2.
#
# A→B isolates the compilation-pipeline benefit (the ptxas-tuning flags);
# B→C isolates the autotuner's knob benefit; A→C is the total. fast-math is
# held IDENTICAL across A/B/C (production B uses it — see setup.py:643), so
# A→B is purely the ptxas-tuning flags, not a numerics confound.
# ==========================================================================

# Structural -D the bench TU needs to compile at d=2048 (mirrors
# tuning/decoder_bench.build_variant: the d!=128 bench branch). NOT opt flags.
_BENCH_STRUCTURAL = [
    "-DSG_TUNED_GEMM_IMPL=1",     # select the wgmma cell driver
    "-DSG_DEC_BENCH_LAYOUT=1",    # → the _DEC_BENCH_D=2048 layout branch
    "-DSG_DEC_SCALAR_MEGAKERNEL=0",  # gate off the legacy scalar megakernel
                                     # (its smem grows with d and ptxas
                                     # hard-stops at d>=768; never driven here)
]
_BENCH_GENCODE = ["-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=sm_90a",
                  "-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=compute_90a"]
_BENCH_TU = os.path.join(ROOT, "csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc.cu")


def _vanilla_bench_nvcc(fast_math: bool) -> list:
    """Variant A — what a competent dev would hand-write: -O3 [+--use_fast_math]
    -arch=sm_90a + the structural defines. Explicitly NONE of compile.py's
    ptxas micro-tuning (no --register-usage-level / --def-load-cache /
    --def-store-cache / --extra-device-vectorization / -Xfatbin -compress-all /
    --opt-level=3 / -v)."""
    flags = ["-O3", "-std=c++17", "--expt-relaxed-constexpr"]
    if fast_math:
        flags.append("--use_fast_math")
    return flags + _BENCH_GENCODE + _BENCH_STRUCTURAL


def _augmented_bench_nvcc() -> list:
    """Variants B/C — the EXACT production compile.py flag line for this single
    TU on this toolchain: NVCC_DEVICE_BASE + the CUDA-version-gated ptxas
    tuning ladder (probed live) + grokking's project flags (--use_fast_math
    -DNDEBUG -lineinfo), exactly as setup.py composes it. fast-math ON to match
    A (and production)."""
    from grokking_optimizers.compile import (NVCC_DEVICE_BASE,
                                             _newer_compiler_flags)
    base = list(NVCC_DEVICE_BASE)
    # The CUDA-version-gated additions (register-usage-level=10 on 12.3+,
    # def-load-cache=ca, def-store-cache=wb, --threads, --diag-suppress, …) —
    # the SAME ladder the production/autotuner device compile uses.
    # _newer_compiler_flags returns (extra_host, extra_device); take device.
    try:
        _host, gated = _newer_compiler_flags("sm_90")
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - never block the comparison
        sys.stderr.write(f"[nvcc-baseline] WARN: _newer_compiler_flags failed "
                         f"({exc}); proceeding with NVCC_DEVICE_BASE only\n")
        gated = []
    # grokking project flags (setup.py:643) + bench structural + gencode.
    return (base + list(gated) + ["--use_fast_math", "-DNDEBUG", "-lineinfo"]
            + _BENCH_GENCODE + _BENCH_STRUCTURAL)


def _build_bench_variant(label: str, nvcc_flags: list, splitk: int,
                         fast_math: bool, verbose: bool):
    """JIT-build the d=2048 decoder bench TU with a fully-specified nvcc flag
    set + a dW split-K override. Distinct module name + build dir so the three
    variants coexist (and never touch the production _ops.so)."""
    from torch.utils.cpp_extension import load as _load
    flags = list(nvcc_flags) + [f"-DSG_TUNED_DEC_DW_SPLITK={splitk}"]
    name = f"mega_decoder_d2048_task11_{label}_sk{splitk}"
    bdir = os.path.join("/workspace", "task11_bench_build", f"{label}_sk{splitk}")
    os.makedirs(bdir, exist_ok=True)
    os.environ.setdefault("TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST", "9.0a")
    cxx = ["-O3", "-std=c++17"]
    if fast_math:
        cxx.append("-ffast-math")
    sys.stderr.write(f"[nvcc-baseline][{label}] split-K={splitk} fast_math={fast_math}\n")
    sys.stderr.write(f"[nvcc-baseline][{label}] nvcc flags: {' '.join(flags)}\n")
    mod = _load(name=name, sources=[_BENCH_TU],
                extra_include_paths=[ROOT],
                extra_cuda_cflags=flags,
                extra_cflags=cxx,
                build_directory=bdir,
                verbose=verbose)
    return mod


def _time_bench_seed(DB, mod, d: int, batch: int, seed: int,
                     reps: int, warmup: int, iters: int):
    """Median step-ms for ONE seed: inputs reseeded per-seed (params/tokens from
    a per-seed generator — the genuine 3-seed coverage, vs decoder_bench.measure
    which hardcodes seed 42). Shapes/work are identical across seeds, so this is
    the protocol's timing-variance probe at the d=2048 roofline (correctness +
    determinism are the SEPARATE fp64 gate). Mirrors roofline_bench.time_seed."""
    import time as _t
    dev = torch.device("cuda")
    total = int(mod.TOTAL)
    vocab, seq = int(mod.VOCAB), int(mod.SEQ)
    g = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(seed)
    params = (torch.randn(total, generator=g, device=dev) * 0.02).contiguous()
    tokens = torch.randint(0, vocab, (batch, seq), generator=g,
                           device=dev).to(torch.int32).contiguous()
    targets = torch.randint(0, vocab, (batch,), generator=g,
                            device=dev).to(torch.int32).contiguous()
    state = torch.zeros(3 * total, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
    lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd = 1e-3, 0.9, 0.98, 1e-8, 0.0
    bc1, bc2 = 1.0 - beta1, 1.0 - beta2

    def call():
        return mod.tc_train_step(params, tokens, targets, state, lr, beta1,
                                 beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2, 1, 0)

    for _ in range(warmup):
        call()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    walls = []
    for _ in range(reps):
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        t0 = _t.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(iters):
            call()
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        walls.append((_t.perf_counter() - t0) / iters * 1e3)
    return statistics.median(walls), [round(w, 4) for w in walls]


def _run_d2048_3point(args) -> int:
    """A/B/C build + 3-seed median step-ms + TF/s + deltas at d=2048."""
    import tuning.decoder_bench as DB
    import time as _time
    fast_math = not args.strict_math
    d, batch = 2048, args.batch
    assert batch % 16 == 0, "B must be divisible by 16"

    variants = [
        ("A", "regular-nvcc (vanilla flags, split-K=4)",
         _vanilla_bench_nvcc(fast_math), 4),
        ("B", "compile.py-default (augmented flags, split-K=4)",
         _augmented_bench_nvcc(), 4),
        ("C", "compile.py-tuned (augmented flags, split-K=2)",
         _augmented_bench_nvcc(), 2),
    ]
    seeds = [int(s) for s in args.seeds.split(",") if s.strip()]
    results = {}
    for label, desc, nvcc_flags, splitk in variants:
        sys.stderr.write(f"\n[nvcc-baseline] ===== variant {label}: {desc} =====\n")
        t0 = _time.perf_counter()
        mod = _build_bench_variant(label, nvcc_flags, splitk, fast_math,
                                   args.verbose_build)
        build_s = _time.perf_counter() - t0
        assert int(mod.D) == d, f"variant {label} compiled D={int(mod.D)} != {d}"
        flops = DB._decoder_gemm_flops_per_step(
            d, batch, int(mod.LAYERS), int(mod.SEQ), int(mod.VOCAB))
        per_seed, per_seed_walls = {}, {}
        for s in seeds:
            med_s, walls = _time_bench_seed(DB, mod, d, batch, s, args.reps,
                                            args.warmup, args.iters)
            per_seed[s] = med_s
            per_seed_walls[s] = walls
        med = statistics.median(per_seed.values())
        tf_s = flops / (med / 1e3) / 1e12
        rec = {"variant": label, "desc": desc, "split_k": splitk,
               "fast_math": fast_math, "d": d, "B": batch,
               "total_params": int(mod.TOTAL), "build_s": round(build_s, 1),
               "per_seed_median_ms": {s: round(per_seed[s], 4) for s in seeds},
               "per_seed_walls_ms": per_seed_walls,
               "across_seed_median_ms": round(med, 4),
               "achieved_tf_s": round(tf_s, 3),
               "pct_roofline": round(100.0 * tf_s / 989.0, 3)}
        results[label] = rec
        sys.stdout.write("VARIANT " + json.dumps(rec) + "\n")
        sys.stdout.flush()

    # Deltas (negative = faster). A→B = pipeline/flags; B→C = autotuner; A→C = total.
    a, b, c = (results[k]["across_seed_median_ms"] for k in "ABC")
    deltas = {
        "A_to_B_pipeline_flags_pct": round(100.0 * (b - a) / a, 3),
        "B_to_C_autotuner_pct": round(100.0 * (c - b) / b, 3),
        "A_to_C_total_pct": round(100.0 * (c - a) / a, 3),
    }
    sys.stdout.write("DELTAS " + json.dumps(deltas) + "\n")
    sys.stdout.flush()
    return 0


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--model", default="decoder")
    ap.add_argument("--opt", default="adamw")
    ap.add_argument("--seeds", default="42,7,123")
    ap.add_argument("--warmup", type=int, default=10)
    ap.add_argument("--iters", type=int, default=30)
    ap.add_argument("--reps", type=int, default=5)
    ap.add_argument("--strict-math", action="store_true",
                    help="Drop --use_fast_math too (the strictest vanilla "
                         "baseline). Default keeps --use_fast_math, isolating "
                         "ONLY compile.py's ptxas micro-tuning.")
    ap.add_argument("--bench-d2048", action="store_true",
                    help="Task-#11 d=2048 roofline 3-point comparison: build "
                         "the decoder bench TU at d=2048 three ways (A vanilla "
                         "nvcc / B compile.py-default / C compile.py-tuned) and "

    for s in args.seeds.split(","):

    c = dict(g.DEFAULT_CONFIG)
    c.update({"model_type": model, "use_amp": False, "use_fused": True,
              "compile_model": False, "matmul_precision": "bf16", "seed": seed,

    bf16-TC kernel 2nd backward vs this fp64-bf16-faithful 2nd backward differ only by the bf16
    floor (the SAME design floor the looksam sam_dir 2e-2 tol calibrates), so sharpness is
    checked at that floor. A SKIPPED SAM phase (sharpness≈0) fails the liveness assert."""
    if model == "decoder":
        from tests.hw.test_decoder_tc import _bf16_faithful_oracle as _orc
        B = int(tx.shape[0]); B16 = B - (B % 16)
        a0 = tx[:B16].to(torch.long); a1 = ty[:B16].to(torch.long)
        named_d = {n: p.detach() for n, p in named_ref}

"""Phase-1 per-cell runtime baseline primitive (counter-free).

Usage: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=i python time_cell.py <opt> <model> [warmup iters reps]
Prints one JSON line."""
import os, sys, json, statistics, traceback
os.environ.setdefault("GATE_SEED", "42")
import torch
sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/SuperGrok1.5")

def main():
    opt, model = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    warmup = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 15
    iters  = int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 50
    reps   = int(sys.argv[5]) if len(sys.argv) > 5 else 7
    rec = {"opt": opt, "model": model}

        g, c, m, data, dev = G._build_cell(model)
        tx, ty = data[0], data[1]
        spec = G._CELLS[f"{opt}/{model}"]
        cc = {}
        def step(s):
            return fused_train_step(model, opt, m, opt_obj, tx, ty,
                                    state_cache=cc, step=s, return_grad=False,
                                    gemm_impl="wgmma")
        opt_obj = spec["factory"](g, m.parameters(), c)
        l0 = step(1)
        for s in range(2, warmup + 2):
            step(s)
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        med = []
        st = warmup + 2
        for r in range(reps):
            e0 = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True); e1 = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
            e0.record()

            e1.record(); torch.cuda.synchronize()

def _sccache_env() -> Dict[str, str]:
    """Detect ccache (preferred for host TUs) and sccache (preferred for
    NVCC), wire whichever is present. Honour ``SCCACHE_REDIS_ENDPOINT``
    if set (§12 I1 — Redis-backed shared cache across hosts).

    The host CC/CXX get ccache when it's on PATH (3-4.5× faster than
    sccache on local C/C++ object retrieval per the sccache project's
    own measurements). NVCC always goes through sccache when sccache is
    on PATH (after vllm#13697 the CUDA hash bug is fixed)."""
    out: Dict[str, str] = {}
    ccache = shutil.which("ccache")
    sccache = shutil.which("sccache")

    if ccache:
        host_dir = _writable_cache_dir("ccache")
        shim = _ccache_masquerade_dir(ccache)
        if host_dir is not None and shim is not None:
            out["CCACHE_DIR"] = str(host_dir)
            out["PATH"] = f"{shim}{os.pathsep}{os.environ.get('PATH', '')}"
            out["CC"]  = _masquerade_compiler_name(shim, ccache, "CC",  "cc")
            out["CXX"] = _masquerade_compiler_name(shim, ccache, "CXX", "c++")

    if sccache:
        sc_dir = _writable_cache_dir("sccache")
        if sc_dir is not None:
            out.setdefault("SCCACHE_DIR", str(sc_dir))
            if "CXX" not in out:
                shim = _ccache_masquerade_dir(sccache)
                if shim is not None:
                    out["PATH"] = f"{shim}{os.pathsep}{os.environ.get('PATH', '')}"
                    out["CC"]  = _masquerade_compiler_name(shim, sccache, "CC",  "cc")
                    out["CXX"] = _masquerade_compiler_name(shim, sccache, "CXX", "c++")
            # NVCC through sccache via torch's SUPPORTED knob (PYTORCH_NVCC), NOT
            # CUDA_NVCC_EXECUTABLE (a CMake var cpp_extension ignores). Space-form
            # is safe here — torch writes it verbatim into ninja, never which's it.
            # Wrap the REAL nvcc binary (what torch itself would resolve:
            # $CUDA_HOME/bin/nvcc), not PATH-spelled "nvcc": on pods where the
            # first `nvcc` on PATH is itself a caching wrapper SCRIPT (e.g.
            # /usr/local/sccache-shim/nvcc `exec sccache nvcc`), sccache would
            # be asked to treat a bash script as the compiler and dies with
            # "Compiler not supported" — observed 2026-06-12, it broke every
            # JIT .cu compile. On hosts whose PATH nvcc IS the real binary
            # this resolves to the same compiler as before.
            out["PYTORCH_NVCC"] = f"{sccache} {_resolve_real_nvcc()}"
        for k in ("SCCACHE_REDIS_ENDPOINT", "SCCACHE_REDIS", "SCCACHE_S3_BUCKET"):
            if k in os.environ:
                out[k] = os.environ[k]

    return out


def _compiler_cache_present() -> Tuple[bool, List[str]]:
    """Mandate #8 — which compiler caches are on PATH. Returns
    ``(present, names)`` where names ⊆ {'ccache', 'sccache'}."""
    names = [n for n in ("ccache", "sccache") if shutil.which(n)]

def _writable_cache_dir(name: str) -> Optional[Path]:
    """Prefer /dev/shm/<name> (ramdisk); fall back to ~/.cache/<name>."""
    for candidate in (Path(f"/dev/shm/{name}"), Path.home() / ".cache" / name):
        try:
            candidate.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            probe = candidate / ".probe"
            probe.write_text("ok")
            probe.unlink()
            return candidate

<system-reminder>[Truncated: PARTIAL view — showing lines 1-207 of 501 total (51283 tokens, cap 25000). Call Read with offset=208 limit=207 for the next page, or Grep to find a specific section. Do NOT answer from this page alone if the answer may be further in the file.]</system-reminder>

1	# CODEBASE_EXPLAINED.md — SuperGrok1.5 exhaustive architectural reference
2	
3	> **Purpose.** A single, self-contained reference: a senior engineer should be able to read this and
4	> fully understand how the system works — and resume development — without re-reading the codebase.
5	> Authored 2026-06-17 by 5 parallel deep-readers (read-only, refute-by-default), every concrete claim
6	> cited as `file:line`. Companion docs: `SESSION_STATE.md` (live resume state), `PLANNING_INPUT.md`
7	> (opportunity map + open decisions), `.perf/phase1_status_audit.md` (the audit this was built on).
8	
9	## Overview — the mental model
10	
11	SuperGrok1.5 trains **3 model families** (transformer decoder, ViT, Mamba-3) under **11 optimizers**
12	= **33 cells**, each compiled as a **single fused persistent CUDA megakernel** on H100 (bf16 wgmma).
13	The defining decision: **one kernel launch runs the entire training step** — forward, backward,
14	gradient reduction, *and* the optimizer update — with phases separated only by an in-kernel,
15	hand-built grid barrier. No per-step relaunch, no cooperative launch, optimizer state stays resident.
16	This is the "one binary, one launch" thesis: it removes launch latency and HBM round-trips between
17	ops, at the cost of pinning **one CTA per SM** (the grid barrier needs all CTAs co-resident).
18	
19	`compile.py` is a **superoptimizer / autotuner**: it JIT-builds, fp64-gates, and times flag / macro /
20	structural variants per cell and bakes per-TU winners, with a learned cost-model and an in-loop
21	correctness gate. Every change — by hand or by the autotuner — must clear the **HARD gate**: fp64
22	parity (rel 1e-4; SAM 2.5e-2) **and** A/A/A bit-determinism (identical across 3 runs). Legal rewrites
23	are **transport-only** (they may move data but must preserve the ascending-k fp32 reduction order, so
24	parity + determinism hold); anything that changes numerics is gate-arbitrated under a keep/revert ratchet.
25	
26	**Performance posture (read §4 closely).** At small/medium scale the system is **latency /
27	serialization-bound** — the decoder runs at ~6.5% of the 989 TF/s bf16 roofline at d=2048. That gap is
28	*largely fixable* (grid-barrier serialization, sub-cuBLAS hand-rolled wgmma, non-GEMM work serialized
29	rather than overlapped, 1-CTA/SM occupancy), **not** a non-GEMM physics floor. The design goal is a
30	high roofline % at **every** scale; the files are meant to optimize for the project they are dropped into.
31	
32	## Contents
33	1. **The model megakernels (decoder / vit / mamba3) + the L3-TC substrate** — the persistent kernel, the GridBarrier, the wgmma + cp.async-ring substrate, the phase structure, per-model specifics.
34	2. **The optimizer files (the 11 optimizers + the fused P3 tail)** — the one-launch fusion, opt_id dispatch, per-optimizer mechanisms (incl. the SuperGrok family), the perf + correctness reality.
35	3. **compile.py — the superoptimizer / autotuner** — the search, the in-loop fp64 gate, macro-injection + drift guard, the Level-2 work, portability, the build env.
36	4. **Why it is latency-bound + the roofline reality + the perf methods** — the measured numbers, the phase breakdown, the mechanisms, the scale-dependence, the keep/revert ratchet.
37	5. **The correctness methodology** — the fp64 + A/A/A HARD gate, transport-only rewrites, the ratchet, the fake-green / oracle-trust hazards and how they are caught.
38	
39	---
40	
41	## The model megakernels (decoder / vit / mamba3) + the L3-TC substrate
42	
43	This section documents the heart of the system: the three per-model persistent megakernels and the hand-built Hopper tensor-core substrate (wgmma + cp.async ring + grid barrier) they all share. Every concrete claim cites `file:line`.
44	
45	### 1. The persistent-megakernel design — one `__global__` per train step
46	
47	The defining structural decision is that an *entire training step* — forward pass, backward pass, gradient reduction, and the optimizer update — runs inside **one** `__global__` kernel launch, with phases separated only by in-kernel grid barriers. There is **no per-step relaunch** and **no cooperative launch**.
48	
49	- **Decoder** entry point: `fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<Opt>` (`csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:672-678`) launched by `launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<Opt>` (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:1511-1569`). The plain triple-chevron launch `fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<Opt><<<grid, block, dyn_smem, stream>>>` (`:1566`) is an ordinary kernel launch — **not** `cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel`.
50	- **ViT**: `fused_vit_megakernel_tc<Opt>` / `launch_fused_vit_megakernel_tc` (`csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_vit_megakernel.cuh:1178`).
51	- **Mamba3**: `fused_mamba_megakernel_tc<Opt>` (`csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_mamba_megakernel.cuh:527-532`), launched at `fused_mamba_megakernel.cuh:349`.
52	
53	The host-side seams that wire these into the Python `_ops` extension are the `*_launcher.cu` TUs: `mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu`, `mega_vit_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu`, `mega_mamba_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu`. Each exposes ONE non-template host launcher with a plain pointers/ints + `FusedScalars` POD boundary so `dispatch.cpp` can `extern`-declare it without any header-only types crossing the ABI (`mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu:14-24`). The launcher TU exists specifically because the Fork-B TC cell driver (`mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc.cu`) owns its own `PYBIND11_MODULE` and is dropped from `_ops` by `setup.py`'s `_collect()` (PyInit collision) — so without this globbed-in seam the bf16 race path had no way to reach the TC kernel and silently ran eager (`:5-11`). The launcher is compiled per-TU with `-DSG_TUNED_GEMM_IMPL=1` (`mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu:30`) to select the wgmma branch.
54	
55	**Grid shape: gridDim.x == #SMs, one persistent CTA per SM.** The launcher reads the SM count via `cudaDeviceGetAttribute(..., cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount, ...)` and launches exactly that many CTAs: `launch_ctas = (unsigned)n_sms; ctx.n_ctas = launch_ctas` (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:1547-1549`). The optional `ncta_cap` argument (default 0 = full saturation; the race always passes 0) lets a memory-constrained test launch fewer CTAs (`:1504-1510`).
56	
57	**Why one CTA/SM.** The grid barrier (below) rendezvouses all `n_ctas` CTAs at every phase boundary; this can only complete if every launched CTA is *simultaneously resident*. So the launcher hard-gates occupancy ≥ 1 with the *actual* dynamic smem and **refuses to launch otherwise** rather than risk a hang: `cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor(...); if (occ < 1) return cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources` (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:1540-1545`). The scalar fallback launcher makes the rationale explicit in its assert: "0 blocks/SM — GridBarrier would hang" (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:317-321`). Pinning one CTA per SM (via `sm_id()` reading `%smid`, `megakernel_common.cuh:65-73`) also keeps that SM's optimizer-state slice warm in its L2 partition across the whole step (`megakernel_common.cuh:57-63`).
58	
59	**Why fusion instead of relaunch.** A conventional pipeline relaunches a kernel per op (fwd GEMM, bwd GEMM, dW GEMM, optimizer step), paying launch latency and round-tripping every activation/gradient through HBM between launches. The megakernel keeps activations and the reduced gradient resident in an HBM workspace it owns and never tears down the grid, so the only cross-phase synchronization cost is the in-kernel barrier — no launch overhead, no driver round-trips, and the optimizer state stays L2-resident on its owning SM.
60	
61	**Why not cooperative launch.** Cooperative grid sync (`cooperative_groups::grid_group::sync()`) requires `cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel`, which caps the launchable grid at the number of CTAs that can be co-resident *and is itself subject to the cooperative-launch CTA ceiling*. The hand-built `GridBarrier` (below) needs no cooperative launch, so it "scales past the cooperative-grid CTA cap" (`megakernel_common.cuh:27-29`).
62	
63	### 2. The hand-built GridBarrier (`megakernel_common.cuh`)
64	
65	`GridBarrier` (`megakernel_common.cuh:147-255`) is a reusable arrive/wait grid barrier built from **two global atomics plus a sense-reversing generation counter**:
66	
67	- `g_arrived` — count of CTAs that have reached the current barrier.
68	- `g_generation` — the sense-reversing generation, advanced once each time the barrier is crossed (`:148-150`).
69	
70	All state is host-zero-initialized; the launcher re-zeros all three counters per launch with `cudaMemsetAsync` (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:1557-1559`). `PersistentContext` bundles these device pointers + `n_tasks` + `n_ctas` into the uniform kernel signature (`megakernel_common.cuh:263-276`).
71	
72	**The mechanism** (`GridBarrier::sync()`, `:157-210`):
73	1. `__syncthreads()` so the whole CTA reaches the barrier before its leader publishes.
74	2. Thread 0 samples `my_gen = *(volatile)g_generation` (the sense it is waiting to leave).
75	3. **§1.14 RELEASE**: `__threadfence()` makes this CTA's phase writes visible device-wide *before* arrival is announced (`:166-169`).
76	4. `prev = atomicAdd(g_arrived, 1)`. The CTA whose add completes the set (`prev+1 == n_ctas`) is the **last arriver**: it `atomicExch(g_arrived, 0)` to clear the count for the next phase, `__threadfence()`, then `atomicAdd(g_generation, 1)` — order matters so an observer of the new generation also sees `arrived==0` (`:173-182`).
77	5. **Everyone else spins** on `(volatile)g_generation == my_gen` (`:194-200`).
78	6. **§1.14 ACQUIRE**: after observing the generation advance, `__threadfence()` so peers' released phase writes are visible (`:203-205`), then a closing `__syncthreads()` releases the rest of the block (`:208-209`).
79	
80	**Why sense-reversing beats a naive counter reset.** The classic hazard with a counter barrier is *reuse*: if you just reset `arrived=0`, a fast CTA can enter the *next* barrier and increment the counter before a slow CTA has even observed the release of the *previous* one (`:128-134`). The generation counter fixes this — a late CTA waits for the generation to *advance* (the consumer side never touches `arrived` for reset), so an early CTA cannot lap it.
81	
82	**Why `__nanosleep` backoff.** A tight `volatile`-read spin hammers the L2/memory subsystem and steals issue slots from the still-arriving (laggard) CTAs. The waiter instead parks with `__nanosleep(backoff)` on an exponentially growing nap capped at 1024 ns: `backoff = (backoff < 1024u) ? (backoff << 1) : 1024u` (`:193-199`). This is behavior-preserving — it exits the instant the generation advances; only the *poll cadence* changes (sm_70+; a no-op fallback on older arches).
83	
84	**The fused reset (`sync_reset`, `:222-254`).** The L3 phase loop needs the task-queue counter zeroed between the reduce phase and the optimizer phase. Rather than `sync → reset → sync` (which would cost 4 grid barriers + 2 standalone resets per step), the reset is folded into the last-arriver critical section: the last CTA does `atomicExch(g_arrived,0)` **and** `atomicExch(reset_counter,0)` *before* the release-store that bumps the generation, so any CTA that later observes the new generation is guaranteed to see `reset_counter==0`. This collapses 4 grid barriers → 2 per step with identical ordering/visibility (`:213-221`). It is invoked as `bar.sync_reset(ctx.g_next_task)` (e.g. `fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:953`).
85	
86	**Minimal fences (§1.14).** The doctrine is exactly one `__threadfence()` before the arrival publish and one after the wait — the minimum for a correct release/acquire pair (`:34, 136-142`). A loose extra fence here is "both a correctness and a >10% perf footgun" (`:32-34`).
87	
88	**TaskQueue / work-stealing.** Alongside the barrier, `TaskQueue` (`:91-117`) is a single global atomic counter (`g_next_task`). `next_block(smem_slot)` has the leader thread do one `atomicAdd` and broadcast the claimed parameter-tensor index to the whole CTA via shared memory (`:108-116`). There is no static partition — an idle CTA simply calls `next_block()` again, so a CTA that drains its tensor early steals the next one; the atomic *is* the steal (`:75-90`). Determinism is preserved because the work-steal queue only picks *who* reduces an element range, never the *order* of the fp32 summation within it (see P2 below).
89	
90	### 3. The in-kernel phase structure (decoder TC, the reference layout)
91	
92	The decoder TC kernel body (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:672-1502`) is the canonical 5-phase / 4-barrier layout (`:18-37`); the ViT and Mamba kernels mirror it. Phase-by-phase, with the staged-optimizer insertions:
93	
94	- **P0 (zero + weight pre-stage)** — each CTA zeroes its own LN-vec partials and loss slot (`:810-811`), and converts the fp32 params to the bf16 weight cache `wbf_cache` (C1) grid-strided and element-owned (`dectc_wbf_convert`, `:814`). No host memset; each CTA owns its slice → no cross-CTA contention.
95	- **B0** (`bar.sync()`, `:818`) — fences the bf16 weight cache and zeroed partials before any P1 GEMM reads them.
96	- **(P1 window) embedding list build** — CTA 0 builds the counting-sort token lists *here*, overlapping the other CTAs' fwd/bwd (`dectc_embed_build_lists`, `:828-829`), so the already-present B1 barrier fences it for P2 with **no new barrier**.
97	- **P1 (token-tile fwd+bwd GEMMs)** — each CTA grid-strides over tiles of `kTileM` rows (`:840`); per tile it runs `dectc_forward_tile` → NLL, then `dectc_backward_tile` → writes activations X, output adjoints dY, embedding-input adjoint dh0, and LN-vec partials (`:847-868`). Barrier-free within a tile. Loss accumulated fp32 per CTA into `loss_part[cta]` (`:866, 869`).
98	- **B1** (`:877`) — all activations (X + dY) + LN-vec partials complete.
99	- **P2 (dW GEMM + grad assembly)** — builds the 9 dW specs into shared smem (thread 0; identical for all threads, keeping the spec array off every thread's stack, `:890-897`); runs the dW GEMMs (split-K or single-CTA, §6 below, `:919-931`); then assembles biases (`dectc_dw_biases`), the embedding owner-scan (`dectc_embed_owner_scan`), and the deterministic LN-vec reduce (`dectc_lnvec_reduce`) (`:937-939`). The loss is reduced in **fp64** by CTA 0 only — `double s = Σ loss_part[c]; mean = s/B` — because the 1e-5 loss rel-tol is the tightest gate and fp32-summing ~4191 terms can miss it (`:940-945, 33`).
100	- **B2** = `bar.sync_reset(ctx.g_next_task)` (`:953`) — reduced grad ready; task queue reset for the optimizer phase.
101	- **Optional P2.x staged-optimizer phases**, each `if constexpr`-gated so every other cell is byte-identical:
102	  - **P2.4 SAM 2nd backward** (LookSAM / SuperGrok11/15 / SuperGrok2, `:993-1110`): global ‖g‖ deterministic ascending-CTA reduce → `rho_over_norm`; back up params + perturb `p' = p + (ρ/‖g‖)·g`; re-convert the bf16 cache from `p'`; run a **full second in-kernel fwd+bwd + grad assembly** into a separate `sam_grad` buffer; write the side channel (`sam_dir = g_sam−g` for LookSAM, else `sharpness = (g_sam−g)²`) and restore params from backup. Gated to every-k SAM steps by `st.looksam_sam` (`:995`); on intervening steps the cached side channel is reused.
103	  - **P2.5 grad-norm clip** (GrokAdamW / NeuralGrok, `:1128-1167`): global L2 norm via per-CTA partial → CTA0 ascending sum → `clip_coef`, broadcast; grad is not mutated (the coefficient is applied per-element inside the apply).
104	  - **P2.6 Prodigy d-reduce** (`:1205-1251`): a **fixed-partition** (not work-steal) ascending reduce of the cross-all-tensors (r,s) estimator → EMA decay → `d = max(d_prev, d_coef·r_ema/|s_ema|)`. The fixed partition is deliberate: the older work-steal drain regrouped fp32 sums by timing, an A/A/A determinism violation by construction (`:1182-1203`).
105	  - **P2.7 Muon Newton-Schulz** (`:1268-1322`): grid-cooperative NS orthogonalization of the 11 2D weights, one matrix at a time across all CTAs, barrier-looped per NS iteration (`buf=μ·buf+g → ‖buf‖_F → X=buf·inv_norm → {A=XXᵀ, AX, AAX, orth=aX+bAX+cAAX, swap}×5 → apply`).

107	- **P3 (optimizer tail)** — work-steal the parameter tensors from the (reset) queue; for each, `apply_optimizer<Opt>` over the reduced grad in-place (`:1411-1498`). No barrier after P3 — the kernel exits and the step is complete.

109	The scalar fp32 fallback kernel (`fused_decoder_megakernel<Opt>`, gated by `SG_DEC_SCALAR_MEGAKERNEL`, `:195-292`) shows the same P0→B0→P1→B1→P2→B2→P3 skeleton in its simplest batch-parallel form (each CTA owns a contiguous batch slice, accumulating into a per-CTA `[nCTA × total]` partial, then a deterministic ascending-CTA reduce). It is gated off at large `d` because its per-sample `DecSampleSmem` grows with `SG_DEC_D` and ptxas hard-stops (`:129-138`); the TC engine's `DecTcSmem` is `d`-independent.

113	### 4. The wgmma substrate (`csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/wgmma.cuh`)
114	
115	This is the hand-rolled in-kernel `ss`-wgmma (shared-shared: both operands in smem) for `wgmma.mma_async.sync.aligned.m64nNk16.f32.bf16.bf16`. It deliberately does **not** use CUTLASS — host-launched CUTLASS collectives are not device-callable and are rejected for the persistent-megakernel path (`wgmma.cuh:14-18`). Every asm sequence cites its PTX ISA section (`:28-29`).
116	
117	**Descriptor bit-packing (`make_smem_desc`, `:219-241`).** The 64-bit shared-memory matrix descriptor (PTX §<ip>.4) packs: start address in bits 13:0 (the smem byte address `>>4`, so the low 4 bits must be zero → 16-byte alignment is mandatory or they are silently dropped, `:174-189`), LBO in bits 29:16 (`>>4`), SBO in bits 45:32 (`>>4`), base-offset in 51:49, and the swizzle/layout mode in 63:62 (`:231-235`). The canonical Major-K builders `make_desc_A_kmajor<MN>` / `make_desc_B_kmajor<N>` compute `LBO = MN*16` bytes (one core-matrix block) and `SBO = 128` bytes (8 MN-rows × 16 B/row) for the no-swizzle INTERLEAVE layout, verified against `cute::make_gmma_desc<Major::K>` (`:261-288`).
118	
119	**LayoutType / swizzle encoding (`SwizzleMode`, `:167-172`).** A documented footgun: the layout-type field bits 63:62 are **not** size-ascending — the correct CUTLASS encoding is `NONE=0, SWIZZLE_128B=1, SWIZZLE_64B=2, SWIZZLE_32B=3` (an earlier draft had 32B/128B swapped, `:151-155`). The correctness path ships `kSwizzleNone` (a fully legal mode and the layout the gates validate against torch); 128B-swizzle is a dormant perf-phase template arg (`:156-165`).
120	
121	**Required smem operand layout (`:250-259`).** For an `MN×16` bf16 operand, element `(mn,k)` lives at bf16 index `idx(mn,k) = (k/8)*(MN*8) + mn*8 + (k%8)` — i.e. K=16 is two stacked 8-wide core matrices, each an `MN×8` row-major block of 128-bit rows. The staging loops everywhere (model headers, self-test, tile_pipeline) must write this exact layout.
122	
123	**Fragment decode (`WgmmaAccum<N>` + `wgmma_frag_decode`, `:314-364`).** The per-thread fp32 accumulator holds `N/2` registers (PTX §<ip>.3). The authoritative decode maps `(tid_in_wg, reg i)` → `(row, col)`: the M=64 rows are partitioned warp-major (`row = 16*warp + lane/4 + 8*row_half`), and the N columns are held as n8 column slabs (`col = (lane&3)*2 + col_par + 8*slab`) (`:357-362`). Keeping ONE decode shared by the epilogue store and the gate's reference comparison eliminates the chance of a mismatched private decode (`:310-312`).
124	
125	**Fence/commit/wait choreography (`:366-403`).** `wgmma_fence()` (§<ip>.2) makes prior non-wgmma writes to the accumulator/operand-smem visible before the first issue; `wgmma_commit_group()` (§<ip>.5) batches issued MMAs into a group; `wgmma_wait_group<N>()` (§<ip>.6) blocks until ≤N groups remain — the epilogue must `wait_group<0>` before reading the accumulators.
126	
127	**The ascending-k mainloop (`wgmma_mainloop_kchain`, `:617-644`).** Runs `k_steps` ss-wgmma issues in **fixed ascending k-order** (the DESIGN §3.1 determinism rule: one CTA owns the tile end-to-end, no work-steal split, no float atomics → bit-reproducible). The first issue uses `ScaleD=0` (overwrite, so a fresh accumulator needs no zeroing), the rest `ScaleD=1` (accumulate); one `wgmma_fence()` before the group, one `commit_group()+wait_group<0>()` after. The descriptor generator is a callback `gen(k)`, which is what lets the *same* mainloop serve both the unpipelined gate (fixed pre-staged array) and the pipelined gate (ring-buffer stage) with bit-identical numerics (`:603-609`). The per-N issue overloads (`wgmma_issue_n8/16/32/64/96/128`, `:441-561`) each name exactly `N/2` `+f` accumulator registers; N=128 (default tile, 64 regs) is the in/out/ff GEMM shape.

129	### 5. The cp.async multi-stage ring (`tile_pipeline.cuh` + the PIPE/STAGES macros)
130	
131	`tile_pipeline.cuh` adds the producer/consumer ring choreography on top of the wgmma engine, reusing `Mbarrier`/`cp_async_cg_16`/`cp_async_wait_group` rather than redefining them (`tile_pipeline.cuh:9-17`). It uses **cp.async (`.cg.16`), not TMA** — TMA is explicitly phase-2 (`:199-200`). A `TilePipeline<N,Depth>` (`:142-189`) manages a Depth-stage ring of `(A 64×16 + B N×16)` bf16 tiles plus `2*Depth` mbarriers — a `full[s]` (producer arrives via `arrive_expect_tx` when a stage's loads are issued; consumer waits before wgmma) and an `empty[s]` (consumer arrives when done; producer waits before overwriting, WAR-safe) per stage (`:117-135`). Each barrier expects a **full warpgroup (128) of arrivals** — a per-warp `elect_one` would give 4 arrivals on a count-1 barrier and deadlock the parity wait, a bug called out explicitly (`:170-179`). `tc_pipelined_gemm_m64nNk16` (`:271-364`) splits the 256-thread CTA into WG0 (producer: cp.async-stages each K-tile, `:296-312`) and WG1 (consumer: wgmma in ascending k, `:313-360`), with the `setmaxnreg` register rebalance (producer few regs, consumer many) via `SG_TUNED_PROD_REGS=40 / SG_TUNED_CONS_REGS=232` (`:92-97, 289-294`). Determinism: the consumer issues the SAME ss-wgmma sequence in the SAME ascending-k order, so the pipeline only changes *when* an operand becomes available, not the math (`:265-269`).
132	
133	**The decoder's PIPE/STAGES macros** (`model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh`) wrap this into a tunable 3-way selector:
134	- `SG_TUNED_DEC_GEMM_STAGES` (the base K-loop double-buffer depth; default 2, `:90-92`).
135	- `SG_TUNED_DEC_FWD_PIPE` — master 3-way selector, **baked at 1** (`:185-187`): `0` = the shipped S=2 ring verbatim (byte-identical PTX); `1` = entry (a), the SAME all-threads-stage/WG0-compute ring **deepened** to `SG_TUNED_DEC_FWD_STAGES` slots (more cp.async groups in flight); `2` = entry (b), the full producer/consumer mbarrier engine transcribed from `tile_pipeline.cuh` (`:227-252`). The comment records the tournament verdict: **entry-a deeper ring won (+1.49×); entry-b PIPE=2 LOST (857 vs 618 ms)** (`:186`).
136	- `SG_TUNED_DEC_FWD_STAGES` (2..4), **baked at 4** with PIPE=1 (`:188-190`).
137	
138	`kDecFwdStages = kDecFwdPipe ? FWD_STAGES : kDecTcStages` (`:261`), and `kDecRingStagesMax = max(fwd-ring, dW-ring)` sizes the smem allocation (`:268-269`). The three ring bodies are in `tc_gemm_block_unpipelined`: the producer/consumer mbarrier engine (`:860-987`), the original S=2 double-buffer ring (`:988-1016`), and the deeper RS=3..4 ring (`:1017-1062`). The deeper ring keeps `RS-1` cp.async groups in flight via `cp_async_wait_group<RS-2>` in the steady region (drains the oldest tile) and `<0>` in the tail (`:1032-1061`). At S=2 the deeper loop collapses to `wait_group<0>` exactly, which is why PIPE=0 is byte-clean (`:173-175`).
139	
140	**The dynamic-smem path (`SG_DEC_TC_DYNAMIC_SMEM`).** The static `__shared__ DecTcSmem` is hard-capped at 48 KB on H100 (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:478-485`); the deeper fwd/dX ring's `sA`/`sB` grow ∝ ring depth (`:386-387`) and the legal-max tile reaches 49.64 KB at S=4 (`:460-463`). The preprocessor gate `SG_DEC_TC_DYNAMIC_SMEM = PIPE && (STAGES>2)` (`:464-468`) routes those configs to **dynamic smem** instead: `DecTcSmem` is placed in an `extern __shared__ char[]` pool (`:688-689`), the func is opted into `>48 KB` via `cudaFuncSetAttribute(..., cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, sizeof(DecTcSmem))` (`:1533-1535`), and occupancy ≥1 is certified against the real size against the **228 KB/SM** budget (`:476-477`). This is an allocation change only — identical layout / access pattern / fp32 accumulation order / wgmma issue sequence → parity by construction (`:439-442`). The dW path always keeps the synchronous (lambda-source) staging — it is staging-bound, not drain-bound, so a ring would be the wrong lever (`:782-783`).

142	**The producer/consumer PIPE=2 variant** adds `2*kDecRingStages` mbarrier words `pipe_bars[]` to `DecTcSmem`, but `#if`-gated on the macro so on the shipped PIPE=0|1 builds the member is *entirely absent* and `sizeof(DecTcSmem)`/PTX is byte-identical (`:390-408`). The `SG_DEC_PIPE_BARS_ARG` macro expands to `, sm.pipe_bars` only under PIPE=2 and to nothing otherwise (`:420-424`), so the shipped tile-call sites are textually unchanged. The engine body (`model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:860-987`) makes WG0 the consumer (wgmma into `acc[]`, owns the epilogue) and WG1 the pure producer, with `bar_full`/`bar_empty` mbarriers each expecting 128 arrivals; the consumer issues `issue_k(g_atoms,k,RS)` in ascending k → the wgmma issue sequence and fp32 accumulation are bit-identical to PIPE=0 (`:876-887`).

144	### 6. Decoder specifics
145	
146	- **Causal attention** — `dectc_forward_tile` runs per-sample causal self-attention (`model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:1433`); the head is masked `kj > qi`, in contrast to ViT's bidirectional attention. The final-norm + head + CE run on the **last** position (`kSeq-1`).
147	- **Embedding counting-sort owner-scan** — the embedding gradient is a scatter-add of `dh0` into a small set of vocab rows. The H2 design (`:2418-2446`) uses a deterministic integer counting sort: `dectc_embed_build_lists` (`:2469-2527`) builds CSR offsets `row_start[V+1]` + a permutation `perm[T]` (token positions bucketed by vocab row, ascending-t within each row) once on CTA 0 in the P1 window. The consume `dectc_embed_owner_scan` is a flat grid-stride over all `V·d` output elements where element `(r,j)` walks only row r's tokens in ascending-t order, reading `dh0[perm[i]·d+j]`. This collapses work to `O(d·T)` with coalesced reads and keeps all 132 CTAs busy. **Determinism**: per-row accumulation is the same fixed ascending-t order as the old scan → bit-identical fp32, no atomics (`:2435-2439`). The build's per-(worker,row) cursor uses an ascending-worker prefix within a row so lower-t chunks land first — globally ascending t per bucket (`:2501-2513`).
148	- **dW split-K (`SG_TUNED_DEC_DW_SPLITK`)** — chunks the dW `K=T` contraction across CTAs so the ~62% idle SMs in P2 do real work (`:86-88`). `dectc_dw_run_tile_splitk<N>` (`:2295-2339`) computes a PARTIAL over K-chunk `kc` of `G` into a per-(tile,chunk) scratch slot with a **floor-balanced partition** `k0=floor(kc·KS/G), k1=floor((kc+1)·KS/G)` — near-equal, summing to KS exactly for any KS≥G (a ceil split would leave a trailing empty chunk whose unwritten slot sums garbage; the floor never empties one, `:2288-2294`), with an explicit empty-chunk guard zeroing the slot (`:2318-2322`). `dectc_dw_reduce_splitk` (`:2343-2366`) then sums the G chunk-partials in **ascending kc** → deterministic. The default is now **G=1** (`:101`): with DW_STAGE=1 the single-CTA dW is 2.05× faster than G=2-scalar, making split-K (a scalar-dW grid-fill mitigation) obsolete (`:98-100`).
149	- **The DW_STAGE staging method (`SG_TUNED_DEC_DW_STAGE`, default 1)** — the dW GEMM is **staging-bound, not drain-bound**: ~97% of each K-step was the scalar transposed-strided operand gather, only ~3% the wgmma (`:117-124`). So the lever is faster *staging*, not pipelining the MMA. `SG_TUNED_DEC_DW_STAGE=1` does a cheap grid-cooperative pre-transpose (`dectc_dw_transpose_operands`, `:2088`) writing each weight's dY/X once per step into a **contiguous K-major** scratch (`dYt[Nout,K], Xt[Kin,K]`, K-contiguous + 16B-aligned), so the dW then builds `DecGmemTileSrcA/B` over it and reuses the existing cp.async ring's 16-byte coalesced copies instead of the 2-byte strided gather (`:132-143`). It changes transport only — fp64 parity + A/A/A by construction. `kDecDwTransposeActive = (DW_STAGE==1) && (DW_SPLITK==1)` (`:1994`); when active, an extra B1b barrier fences the transposed operands before any dW GEMM read (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:910-915`).

151	### 7. ViT specifics
152	
153	ViT is a genuine rewrite (separate header `model_stage_vit_tc.cuh`) with four deltas vs the decoder twin (`:21-32`): (1) **full bidirectional attention** — no causal mask, every key contributes for every query (`:22-24, 764`); (2) patch-proj `Linear(49→128)` replaces token embedding, with a learned CLS token prepended at position 0 and a `pos[17]` table; (3) the CLS pos-0 head (final-norm + head + CE run on position 0, not the last); (4) `kSeq=17` forces `kTileM = LCM(17,64) = 1088` (17 stacked m64 atoms = 64 samples × 17 positions).
154	
155	**The B1 sub-tile lever (`SG_TUNED_VIT_P1_SUBTILE_S`, baked at 8).** Because the GEMM tile is locked at 1088 rows, at B=1024 there are only `n_tiles=16` P1 tiles, so **116 of 132 CTAs do zero P1 work and spin at B1** the whole fwd+bwd — tile-count-vs-SM quantization, the #1 ViT cost (51.2% of the step) (`:125-131`). This knob decouples the P1 *scheduling* granularity from the 1088 GEMM lock: P1 grid-strides over sub-tiles of **S whole samples** (`kSeq·S` rows) instead of whole 1088-row tiles, growing `n_tiles` ~`64/S`× so the idle CTAs pick up work and the B1 spin collapses (`:133-137`). S must stay a *whole-sample* count — never split a 17-row sample across CTAs, which would corrupt attention (`:137-141`). The sub-tile row count `kSeq·S` is generally not a multiple of 64, so the small GEMMs pad M up to `ceil(rows/64)·64` atoms with a runtime `m_real` row-guard making the pad rows inert and race-free (`:139-141, 373-391`). **Default 64** (== `kSamplesPerTile`) makes the build byte-identical (the `m_real` guard + runtime-m_atoms code is `#if`'d out at S==64, `:143-147`). The P1 loop using `kVitP1SubtileRows` is at `fused_vit_megakernel.cuh:588-613`. **Parity**: dW/biases/cls/pos grads are byte-identical (P2 reads acts by global token row, contracts ascending-k independent of P1 tiling); the LN-affine γ/β grads + loss are valid fp32 reassociations absorbed by the 1e-4 reorder tol; A/A/A holds because S is a fixed deterministic partition (`:150-162`). The baked verdict: **S=8 is parity-clean (11/11 ViT cells × 3 seeds) and fastest — 4.02× vs S=64 OFF at d=2048/B=1024** (`:164-169`).
156	
157	ViT P2 is dW-output-stationary (`vittc_dw_run_tile` or split-K, `:642-648`) plus biases, the cls/pos owner-scan (`vittc_clspos_owner_scan`, `:656`), and the LN-vec reduce (`:657`).

159	### 8. Mamba3 specifics
160	
161	Mamba3 (`model_stage_mamba3.cuh`) is the genuine Mamba-3 SISO architecture (arXiv 2603.15569, ICLR 2026) transcribed line-for-line from the fp64-verified oracle (`:8-15`). The mixer is a complex **exponential-trapezoidal selective scan** (Eq 25, the heart of the kernel):
162	
163	`v_t = Bbar_t ⊙ x_t; h_t = alpha_t·(R_t@h_{t-1}) + beta_t·(R_t@v_{t-1}) + gamma_t·v_t; y_t = Σ_{c,d} Cbar_t[c,d]·h_t` with `alpha=exp(dt·A), gamma=lam·dt, beta=(1-lam)·dt·alpha` per head and a 2×2 rotation `R(phi)` per complex coord (`:41-46`).
164	
165	**Per-coord state / the seq=8 register exploit.** Parallelization is batch-parallel (Option B, identical to the decoder scalar design): each CTA owns a fixed contiguous batch slice and the whole CTA cooperates on one sample at a time (`:52-62`). The scan exploit: **one thread owns SSM channel `j ∈ [0,d_inner)`**, and within its head holds the complex state `h[Nc][2]` in **registers**, unrolling `t=0..kSeq-1` (`mb_scan_fwd`, `:521-568`). Because seq=8 is tiny, the backward recomputes the forward keeping the full `h_hist`/`v_hist` in registers — **no checkpointing** (`:56-58, 570-574`). A subtle constraint: the per-coord arrays (`hr/hi/vpr/vpi`, `kStateC=64` each) are runtime-indexed local memory, and the c-loop is intentionally *not* `#pragma unroll`'d — a full unroll would force >255 registers and the carried state wouldn't persist across the t-loop (the documented "t=0 right, t>0 wrong" bug, `:527-531`).
166	
167	**Why MambaSampleSmem caps placement at ~d=142.** The per-CTA `MambaSampleSmem` (`:142-202`) caches **both layers'** forward activations (`x_in`, `z`, `Bbar`, `Cbar`, `y_scan`, SwiGLU internals, etc.), and these widths scale with `d`/`d_inner`. The struct exceeds the 48 KB static cap, so it must live in **dynamic smem** opted-in via `cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize(kMambaSmemBytes)` (`:64-68`; `mamba3_layout.cuh:257-264`). At the production `d=128` it is `kMambaSmemFloats=53961` → `kMambaSmemBytes=215844` (~215 KB), pinned by a `static_assert(sizeof(MambaSampleSmem) == kMambaSmemBytes)` (`:206-208`) and bounded by `static_assert(kMambaSmemBytes <= 228*1024)` (`mamba3_layout.cuh:275-278`). Since the live set scales with `d` and is already at ~215 KB of the ~228 KB/SM opt-in budget at `d=128`, the maximum placeable `d` is only marginally above it — roughly `d≈142` before one CTA/SM can no longer place (which would hang the GridBarrier). This is why the `d=1024` bench variant (`SG_MB_BENCH_LAYOUT=1`, `d_inner=2048`, `kMambaSmemFloats=329481` ≈ 1.3 MB, `mamba3_layout.cuh:158-159`) **cannot run on the megakernel** — its smem far exceeds the SM budget. Scaling Mamba to `d=2048` would require draining a cached `LayerAct` buffer / chunking the live set (`mamba3_layout.cuh:275-278`).
168	
169	**The Mamba-3 TC rewrite that dropped the dW machinery.** The Mamba-3 mixer is **scan-dominated** — the projections are a tiny share of the wall — so the "TC" Mamba megakernel deliberately runs the validated **scalar** per-sample fwd+bwd (`mb_forward_sample`/`mb_backward_sample`) batch-parallel into a per-CTA **full-grad** partial, then the deterministic ascending-CTA reduce + the canonical optimizer tail. The wgmma-projection dW machinery (the output-stationary dW GEMMs, split-K partials, dW specs of the decoder/ViT twins) is **bypassed** (`fused_mamba_megakernel.cuh:533-539`). Consequently the workspace carve keeps `acts`/`scratch`/`dw_part` zero-width: `part_base` is the full `[nCTA × total]` partial, not the dW-output-stationary split (`:554-563`). The legacy wgmma Fork-B dW path survives only as commentary; the production Mamba TC path is the scalar scan engine wrapped in the persistent megakernel + grid-barrier substrate.
