Sources: `.perf/phase1_status_audit.md:9-13`; `PLANNING_INPUT.md:16-21`. The decoder GEMM FLOPs/step = **3.961e13** (`decoder_reprofile_coarse.txt:7`). ViT's 4.02× from S=8 is the baked B1 sub-tile win (`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:149-158`, `SESSION_STATE.md:9`); mamba3 cannot place at d=2048 because the megakernel is smem-bound at one CTA/SM (`mamba3_layout.cuh:275-277`, `OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:43`), so its roofline is permanently pinned at d=128.

### The phase breakdown of the 618 ms decoder step

From `decoder_reprofile_coarse.txt:10-21` (clock64 critical-path, median of 3 reps; the summed-phase total 646.1 ms slightly exceeds the 616.4 ms wall — the gap is host/launch + un-stamped slack, `decoder_reprofile_coarse.txt:9`):

| phase | ms | % of summed | what it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P1_fwd** | 178.5 | 27.6% | token-tile forward GEMMs (the cp.async-ring engine) |
| **P1_bwd** | 176.7 | 27.3% | dX backward GEMMs (same ring) |
| **B1_barrier** | 108.4 | 16.8% | grid-sync between P1 (fwd/bwd) and P2 (dW) |
| **P2_dW_GEMM** | 106.7 | 16.5% | weight-gradient GEMMs (operand-staging-bound) |
| **P3_opt_tail** | 38.0 | 5.9% | the fused optimizer update |
| **B2_barrier** | 20.1 | 3.1% | grid-sync into the optimizer tail |
| **P2_grad_asm** | 16.8 | 2.6% | gradient assembly |
| **B0_barrier** | 0.9 | 0.1% | initial grid-sync |

Two aggregates the owner tracks: the **GEMM phases P1_fwd + P1_bwd ≈ 55%** (and adding P2_dW the GEMM-engine phases reach **74.9%** of the wall — verified: (178.5+176.7+106.7)/616.4); and the **grid-barriers B0+B1+B2 = 256.2M cyc ≈ 129.4 ms = 20.0% of summed** (`decoder_reprofile_coarse.txt:21`), which is *pure serialization idle* — the persistent grid-barrier waits on the slowest CTA, so every fast CTA stalls. P3 the optimizer tail is **5.9%**, *not* the "<1%" the early ledger claimed — a real (if minor) headroom item, and the reason the "max the optimizer kernels" surface is non-trivial (`.perf/phase1_status_audit.md:21-24`, `OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:38` documents the earlier mis-framing that the vec4-AdamW lever exposed).

### WHY it is latency-bound — the three mechanisms

This is the load-bearing claim and it is honest: the gap is **fixable inefficiency, not an Amdahl wall of unavoidable non-GEMM compute.**

**(a) The GEMM phases are ~11× slower than the ideal tensor-core time, and the gap is fixable, not compute-Amdahl.** The matmuls' *ideal* TC time is 3.961e13 FLOPs / 989.4 TF/s = **40.0 ms** (verified). Yet the GEMM-engine phases (P1_fwd + P1_bwd + P2_dW) take **~462 ms**. That ~420 ms gap is NOT "the rest is non-GEMM work the roofline can't count" — these phases *are* the GEMM phases. The gap decomposes into four fixable inefficiencies:
- **~20% barrier serialization** — slowest-CTA-gated grid-syncs (above), pure idle, attackable by phase overlap / fewer barriers / async.
- **The hand-rolled persistent wgmma running well below cuBLAS-class efficiency.** The engine lives in the persistent megakernel, so it cannot call a host-launched collective: `csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/mma.cuh` is a real Sm90 TMA+wgmma collective but is "explicitly REJECTED for the persistent-megakernel path" (`PERF_ANALYSIS.md:49-50`) — a host collective can't run device-side inside the persistent grid. So the fix is bringing CUTLASS-class *technique* (multi-stage pipeline, TMA, swizzle, warp-specialization) into the hand-rolled engine, whose primitives already exist.
- **Non-GEMM work serialized rather than overlapped under the matmuls** — the ~10 `__syncthreads`-separated fp32 epilogue passes per layer (bias, GELU, residual, LN) run *between* GEMMs instead of hiding under them (`PERF_ANALYSIS.md:38`, the P1-epilogue-fusion lever).
- **1 CTA/SM giving low occupancy to hide HBM latency.** The persistent grid-barrier *requires* ≥1 CTA/SM — the launcher REFUSES to launch (`cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources`) if occupancy < 1 (`model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:180-181`; mirrored in `fused_mamba_megakernel.cuh:330`, `model_stage_vit.cuh:68`). At exactly one resident CTA/SM there is little latency-hiding slack; this is the structural cost of the no-cooperative-launch / hand-built GridBarrier design.

**(b) It is NOT bandwidth-bound either.** Arithmetic intensities are **3,252–12,239 FLOP/byte** (table above), far past the ~295 FLOP/byte ridge — and HBM traffic is only 0.003–0.16% of 3.35 TB/s (`.perf/phase1_status_audit.md:18`). Both the compute roof (6.48%) and the bandwidth roof are far away, so the step sits in a **third LATENCY regime below both roofs**: it is gated by serialization, drain/wait stalls, and single-CTA occupancy, not by either roofline edge.

**(c) The fwd/dX rings are now WGMMA-COMPUTE-bound, not drain-bound — the deeper-ring KEEP already hid the cp.async drain.** This is the freshest and most important refute. The `--fwd-fine` sub-profiler (`decoder_reprofile_fwdfine.txt:23-37`) splits the GEMM ring into ISSUE(cp.async) / WAIT(drain) / WGMMA(mma) / EPI / BARRIER:
- P1_fwd ring: WGMMA **46.6%** vs WAIT(drain) only **9.9%** → "COMPUTE/EPI-bound → deeper ring unlikely to help" (`:30`).
- P1_bwd(dX) ring: WGMMA **40.2%** vs WAIT **5.8%** → same verdict (`:37`).

Before the deeper-ring KEEP the same profiler showed fwd WAIT 43% vs WGMMA 31% and dX WAIT 56% vs 20% — i.e. it *was* drain-bound, deeper prefetch *was* the right lever, and it worked (`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:64-67`). Now the drain is hidden, so **S>4 buffering is measured-unlikely to help on the decoder** (`PLANNING_INPUT.md:13-14`, `.perf/phase1_status_audit.md:19`). The remaining fwd/dX headroom is in GEMM *efficiency* (tiling / TILE_M / interleave / occupancy / register pressure), not more buffering (`PLANNING_INPUT.md:26-28`).

### The design goal (owner directive): high % of roofline at EVERY scale

The directive is a high roofline fraction at *every* scale, and the diagnosis says that is largely achievable at the large shapes. At d=2048 the decoder's 6.48% is **mostly fixable inefficiency** (barrier serialization, sub-cuBLAS engine, un-overlapped epilogues, one-CTA occupancy) — the realistic target is 30–50%+, established by the proof point that the "~2% roofline was a STAGING artifact, not a hardware ceiling" (`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:61`, the dW-staging win that *doubled* the fraction). The residual **hard floor** is only at the very smallest shapes — d=128 tiny matmuls (mamba3, and the toy gate configs) — where the GEMMs are genuinely too small to fill the tensor cores. Crucially, **the fusion-vs-occupancy trade-off flips sign with scale**: the megakernel's aggressive fusion (one persistent kernel, 1 CTA/SM) pays off at large shapes where the GEMMs dominate and grid-barrier serialization is amortizable, but the same one-CTA/SM constraint that enforces the grid barrier *starves* latency-hiding at the smallest shapes where there isn't enough GEMM work to fill an SM.

### The perf levers + the empirical method

The method is the **keep/revert ratchet** (`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:1-11`): apply → build → **fp64 parity HARD-gate (rel 1e-4; SAM 2.5e-2) + A/A/A bit-determinism** → 3-seed timing at the roofline scale → **KEEP iff faster on 3+ seeds AND parity-clean, else REVERT**. Parity is a *gate, not a tiebreaker*; "neutral" counts as not-positive; every revert is root-caused so the mechanism redirects the next move. This is paired with the **relevance gate / profiling doctrine** — wire each model's per-phase profiler and confirm a lever targets a meaningful share *before* building it (the front-load-profiling that killed a wrong ViT excursion at zero cost, `OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:142-158`).

Levers that **WON**:
- **decoder PIPE=1 / STAGES=4** — deepen the proven cp.async ring: **+1.49× (920 → 618 ms)**, roofline 4.35% → 6.475%, fp64+A/A/A green on 11/11 cells × 3 seeds. Mechanism: fwd/dX were *drain*-bound (confirmed by `--fwd-fine` first, per doctrine), so more in-flight loads hid the WAIT. Unblocked by converting `DecTcSmem` static→dynamic smem (the S=3 ring busts the 48 KB static `__shared__` cap; the 227 KB dynamic cap fits). `OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:63-78`; baked default `model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:185-186`.
- **dW contiguous-layout staging (`SG_TUNED_DEC_DW_STAGE=1`)** — **+2.05×** (1889.8 → 920.7 ms), the campaign's first major structural win, doubling roofline 2.08% → 4.35%. A cheap grid-cooperative pre-transpose writes dY/X once per step into K-contiguous scratch so the dW reuses the proven cp.async ring instead of the scalar transposed-strided gather. **SUPERSEDES** the earlier Track-C split-K=2 KEEP (split-K was a scalar-dW grid-fill mitigation; with fast staging the single-CTA dW wins). `OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:60-61`. Cumulative decoder: 1889 → 618 ms ≈ **3.05× from session start** (`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:73-74`).
- **ViT B1 sub-tile S=8** — **4.02×** (5768 → 1434 ms), B1_barrier 51.2% → 41.9%, the #1 ViT lever; 36/36 gate calls clean (`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:149-158`, `SESSION_STATE.md:9`).

Levers that **LOST** (each root-caused — the mechanistic lessons are the payoff):
- **P0 producer/consumer pipelined dW GEMM (PIPE=2)** — fp64 gate PASSED but perf **REGRESSED −11.6%** (920 → 857-class; the older absolute pair was 1921.8 → 2144.8 ms), and depth-3/4 wouldn't even launch (occupancy < 1 vs the ≥1-CTA/SM grid-barrier invariant). **Root cause: the dW is STAGING-bound (~97% staging, ~3% MMA), not drain-bound** — you cannot hide a 97% staging cost behind a 3% MMA, and the producer/consumer split *reduced* the threads doing the already-slow staging. This is the OPPOSITE of the fwd/dX drain-bound regime, and it redirected the campaign to fix *staging* (the +2.05× DW_STAGE win) instead of pipelining the MMA. `OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:52`. (The producer/consumer PIPE=2 also lost its head-to-head tournament against the deeper-ring STAGES=4, 857 vs 618 ms — `OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:78`, `SESSION_STATE.md:11`.)
- **GEMM interleave IL 2→4** — bench −9.3% (the *fastest* lever found) but **A/A/A determinism FAILED** on all 10 decoder cells at d=128 (4-wide dW group-reduce is non-deterministic on ragged atom counts). It ran fine and faster at d=2048 where atoms divide evenly, so the bench *missed* it; the gate caught it. **KEY LESSON: bench-first is necessary but NOT sufficient — every winner must clear the full A/A/A gate.** `OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:37`.
- **ViT dW staging twin** — the verbatim decoder-2× port to ViT: only **+4.5%** (ViT dW is just 3% of its step → not dW-bound) AND fp64+A/A/A gate-RED on supergrok2/vit; reverted. This + the mamba M0 defer crystallized the **META-LESSON: the decoder GEMM-staging win does NOT generalize** — ViT is non-GEMM-surface / B1-load-imbalance-bound, mamba is scan-bound; profile each model's actual bottleneck before picking its lever. `OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:80-105, 142-147`.

Confirmed dry wells (do not re-pursue): optimizer P3-tail micro-opts (vec4 NEUTRAL, the tail is a small share), GEMM-tile knob cycling (converged — TILE_N=64 +51% slower, IL=4 broke A/A/A), and further batch/d scaling on the current code (decoder is the same ~2% at d=1024 and d=2048 → scale-invariant cap; the wins live in the structural levers, not in scaling). `OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:39-44`, `PERF_ANALYSIS.md:46`.

## The correctness methodology (the HARD gate, transport-only rewrites, the ratchet)

This system is an aggressive performance project — a hand-built persistent megakernel, an autotuner that rewrites kernels, and a long series of structural perf levers — bolted onto a correctness contract that *never* moves. The discipline that makes that safe is a single non-negotiable **HARD gate** plus a **keep/revert ratchet** layered on top of it, and a hard-won catalogue of *fake-green* hazards that the gate machinery is specifically shaped to catch. Everything below is the "how do we know a change is correct, and how do we decide whether to keep it" half of the project.

### The HARD gate: fp64 parity + A/A/A bit-determinism

Every change must clear two checks, ANDed together, before it can be considered at all. The canonical statement of the verdict rule is in the ledger header: *"apply → build → fp64 parity HARD-gate + A/A/A determinism → 3-seed timing at the roofline scale → KEEP iff faster on 3+ seeds AND parity-clean, else REVERT. Parity/determinism is a gate, not a tiebreaker"* (`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:5-8`).

**(1) fp64 parity.** The bf16 wgmma megakernel is compared against a *pure-fp64* ground-truth oracle, run at the same shape, with the kernel's bf16 stays the compute precision and fp64 used only as the yardstick (`tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:11-13`). The per-cell harness `run_cell_gate` (`test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:1062`) runs one production L3-TC step through the exact route the race takes (`fused_train_step(..., gemm_impl="wgmma")`, `:1103-1105`), captures the TC-reduced grad and post-step params, and compares against the **canonical fp64 transcription** of the same single source the kernel compiles from (`csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h` → `ref_<opt>_step` in `test_reference_parity.py`, imported at `:1133-1135`). The comparison is structured in two surfaces:
- **(1a) params**, max-relative, default tolerance **1e-4** (`param_tol`, `:1346-1347`). 1e-4 is the *fp32-reorder band*: the kernel's elementwise tail rounds in fp32 in a different association order than the fp64 reference, and 1e-4 is the documented envelope for that (`:1336-1337`). Cells whose update goes through a non-tail numeric path widen it deliberately and document why: Muon's 2D weights run a 5-iteration Newton–Schulz that accumulates ~2e-3 fp32-vs-fp64, so muon uses `param_tol=2e-3` (`:399,408,1342-1345`).
- **(1b) state**, the *decisive* check, tolerance **1e-4** on `[m|v|extra]` (`:1369`). The docstring at `:1352-1359` explains why state, not params, is load-bearing: at step 1 every Adam-family tail collapses to ≈sign(g_amp) in the param update, so (1a) is blind to per-layer β1, amplification magnitude, and *state initialization* — all of which live in the state, not the sign. The grokfast `ema=g0` cold-start is the worked example: a kernel that inited `ema=0` matches params but diverges ~50× in the ema slice (`:1356-1359`).

The SAM-tier surfaces carry a *floor* tolerance instead of the reorder band, because a second backward through a bf16 kernel cannot reach fp32 reorder: **SAM sharpness/sam_dir use 3e-2 / 2.5e-2** (`test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:27-28`, `:439,445,476`). These are explicitly the bf16-TC-vs-pure-fp64 *measured floor* (~2.2e-2 sharpness / 1.87e-2 sam_dir), with the tol set above it (`:634,730`). The looksam sam_dir check is fed the kernel's *own* cached direction and validated against a pure-fp64 second backward perturbed by `ron·g` (`:1161-1224`), with a liveness assert that the oracle direction is `>1e-6` so the parity can never be vacuously satisfied by a skipped SAM phase (`:1222-1224`).

**(2) A/A/A bit-determinism.** The production step is re-run 3× from the same init with fresh state, and loss/grad/params must be **bit-identical** under `torch.equal` (`:1396-1411`). This is `torch.equal` exactly — not a tolerance — across `(L1==L2==L3)`, `equal(G1,G2)`, `equal(P1,P2)` (`:1410-1411`); the SAM cells extend it to `mu` and `sharpness` slices (`:866-869`). Determinism is achieved by *construction*, not luck: fixed batch→CTA ownership and ascending-CTA / ascending-k fp32 reduction order (`tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:6-7`; the mechanism is spelled out in `csrc/fused/sm_90/dec_weights.cuh:59-79` — fixed contiguous batch slices, single-writer per-element owner, one grid barrier, then a cross-CTA reduce summing partials *in ascending CTA index*).

The two checks are ANDed (`ok = tail_ok and det_ok`, `:1417`), and that conjunction is the HARD gate. The autotuner is wired to the *same* gate: `_default_correctness_hook` (`compile.py:7215`) builds a `pick_winner` hook that re-runs `run_cell_gate` and demotes any candidate that fails either leg, fail-closed (a raising hook is treated as a demotion, `:7250-7251,7277`). This was added precisely because the tuner's own timing oracle is fp32 self-consistency, which two co-wrong kernels can both pass — see the IL=4 hazard below.

### Transport-only legal rewrites vs NEEDS-PARITY changes

The rewrite rule that lets the project move fast: **a rewrite may reorder data movement freely, but it must PRESERVE the ascending-k fp32 reduction order.** If it does, bit-determinism and parity hold automatically and the change is *transport-only* — no re-gating drama. If it changes the numeric association, it is **NEEDS-PARITY**: it produces a valid-but-different fp32 reassociation that the gate must arbitrate against the 1e-4 reorder band.

Concrete examples the codebase ships:

- **ViT B1 sub-tiling (`SG_TUNED_VIT_P1_SUBTILE_S`)** is the canonical worked case. Decoupling P1 *scheduling* granularity from the 1088-row GEMM tile changes which global rows land in which CTA. The kernel comment classifies the surfaces precisely (`model_stage_vit_tc.cuh:150-162`): dW / biases / cls / pos grads are **byte-identical** (P2 reads activations by global token row and contracts ascending-k independent of P1 tiling, and each row is a sample-local function preserved by the whole-sample invariant), but the 10 LN-affine γ/β grads and the loss are **valid fp32 REASSOCIATIONS** — regrouping which rows sum into which CTA shifts the low bits — *"absorbed by the gate's 1e-4 fp32-reorder tol (the decoder already ships TILE_M 64/256 through the same gate)."* A/A/A still holds because S is fixed across the 3 runs (a fixed deterministic partition). The explicit conclusion: *"OFF = byte-identical; ON = a NEEDS-PARITY swept dim, the GPU fp64 + A/A/A gate is the arbiter"* (`:161-162`). The whole-sample invariant is a hard `static_assert` (`:239`).

- **decoder `SG_TUNED_TILE_M` 64/256** is the named precedent the ViT comment leans on: changing the token-tile row count is a valid fp32 reassociation of the same reduction, lands inside 1e-4, and the decoder already ships those alternates through the same gate (`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:40` records TILE_M→256 as SKIP +27.7% *on perf*, i.e. it was parity-legal and only lost on speed).

- **split-K dW (`SG_TUNED_*_DW_SPLITK`, factor G)** is the transport-only case that *does* preserve order. Splitting a tile's K-contraction across G CTAs adds parallelism, but the partials are summed by *"a deterministic ascending-chunk reduce ... no float atomics, fixed order → parity + A/A/A bit-determinism hold"*, and `G==1` routes to the byte-identical single-CTA path (`model_stage_vit_tc.cuh:97-104`; `fused_vit_megakernel.cuh:394`). Because the summation order is preserved, split-K is a transport-only rewrite — which is why it could be *kept* (decoder DW split-K 4→2, `OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:36`).

The same "order lives in the summation, not who computes it" principle governs the cross-CTA optimizer reductions (Prodigy's global-d, GrokAdamW's grad-norm clip, Muon's Frobenius norm): they were deliberately moved off the *work-stealing task queue* (whose claim order varies run-to-run → non-associative fp32 regrouping → A/A/A violation) onto a **fixed contiguous element range per CTA + ascending-CTA owner-sum** (`fused_vit_megakernel.cuh:874-888`). The IL=4 reject (below) is the cautionary case where this discipline was violated.

### The keep/revert ratchet (the P-series discipline)

Once a change is parity-clean, perf decides its fate, and the rule is asymmetric on purpose: **parity is a hard gate; perf must be better on 3+ seeds to KEEP, else REVERT** (`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:5-8`). "Neutral" (no measurable gain) counts as not-positive and reverts. On any revert, the *mechanism* is root-caused and used to redirect the next decision (`:8`). The ledger is the canonical record of every KEEP / REVERT / NEUTRAL / SKIP with its why; representative entries:
- **KEEP**: decoder cp.async-ring −14.2% across all decoder cells (`Track A` 0005, `:24`); decoder DW split-K 4→2 −2.5% (`:36`); the Track-E dW staging fix 2.05× (`:61`).
- **REVERT**: vit SAM-scoped outline +5% slower (`:22`); the P0 decoder dW pipelined GEMM — *fp64 gate PASSED (correct), but perf regressed −11.6%*, root-caused to the dW being staging-bound not drain-bound, which then *redirected* the campaign to staging (`Track E` P0, `:52`).
- **REJECT** with the sharpest lesson: decoder GEMM interleave 2→4 was the **fastest** lever found (bench −9.3%) but **A/A/A FAILED** on all 10 decoder cells (IL=4 makes the dW M-atom groups 4-wide and the ragged atom counts make the 4-wide group-reduce non-deterministic). It ran fine and faster at d=2048 where atoms divide evenly, *so the bench missed it; the gate caught it.* The recorded takeaway: *"bench-first is necessary, NOT sufficient — every winner must clear the full A/A/A gate"* (`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:37`).

The structural safety net under the ratchet is **byte-identical OFF defaults for risky knobs**: a NEEDS-PARITY knob must `#if`-erase to the exact pre-knob kernel when off, so a never-engaged lever is provably inert. ViT subtile-S at the default value compiles the m_real row-guard and runtime-m_atoms code out entirely → *"the OFF build is BYTE-IDENTICAL"* (`model_stage_vit_tc.cuh:143-146`, guarded by `#if SG_TUNED_VIT_P1_SUBTILE_S < 64` at `:391`); split-K `G==1` takes the no-scratch single-CTA path (`model_stage_vit_tc.cuh:103-104`); the GEMM interleave width 1 is the bit-for-bit serial path (`:117`). This is what lets the autotuner expand the search space without risking the shipped default.

### Fake-green / oracle-trust hazards (and how they are caught)

The recurring failure mode this project keeps hitting is not a wrong kernel that *fails* a gate — it is a **fake-green**: a gate that passes while the thing it claims to verify is broken, usually because the oracle co-derives with the kernel or the discriminating instrument never runs. The standing audits (`.perf/oracle_trust_audit.json`, `.perf/test_coverage_gap_audit.json`) exist to hunt this class. The catalogue:

- **The macro-drift guard (table-vs-header).** The autotuner emits `-DSG_TUNED_*` flags from a hand-maintained `MACROS` table; if that table drifts from the kernels' `#ifndef SG_TUNED_*` guards, the tuner emits a `-D` no kernel reads (a silent no-op) or misses one. `header_default_macros()` (`_tuned_inject.py:198-208`) declares the asserted defaults, and `setup.py:_verify_macro_names` (`:944-970`) programmatically scans *all* of `csrc/` for the `#ifndef` guards and warns on any table macro not guarded anywhere. The audit note at `_tuned_inject.py:949-953` records *why* this had to become a tree-walk: the old single-file check pointed at a header (`kernels/sm_90/adamw_sm90.cuh`) deleted in the L3-TC-only cut, so it silently early-returned and *could never fire* — itself a fake-green.

- **The SG11 co-wrong oracle (cos operand).** The historical incident class: the kernel computing `cos(grad, MU)` instead of canonical `cos(grad, MOMENTUM)` as the gate's second cosine operand (`oracle_trust_audit.json` finding 2). The cold step-1 gate is *structurally blind* to it: at step 1 `m0=0 ⇒ cos=0 ⇒ gate=sigmoid(0)=0.5` regardless of the operand (`test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:798-803`), and at the default `rescale=0.1` the gate-dependent surfaces are damped below the 1e-4 param tol by Adam v-normalization. The catching instrument is `run_sg11_warmup_gate` (`:882`), which runs warm-up steps so `momentum≠0 ∧ mu≠0` genuinely diverge, pumps `rescale=2.0` so the term is above tolerance (`:919`), recovers the kernel's gate and asserts it matches `cos(grad,momentum)` AND *not* `cos(grad,mu)` — `gate_ok = (err_vs_momentum < 1e-2) and (err_vs_mu > 1e-1)`, two regimes separated by ~3 orders of magnitude (`:1009-1013`), with a non-vacuity assert that the warm-up actually exercised the divergence (`gate_div > 1e-4`, `:1054-1057`). The oracle-trust audit's *open* finding is that this discriminating test is **CLI-only (`--sg11-warmup`)** and never collected by pytest/CI (`oracle_trust_audit.json` finding 2; `test_coverage_gap_audit.json` RG1), so the CI path is still structurally pinned to gate=0.5 — a live coverage gap, not yet closed.

- **The autotune-hook d=128-vs-d=2048 scale lie.** `_default_correctness_hook`'s docstring promises *"PRODUCTION-scale (d=2048)"* validation (`compile.py:7220-7222`) and the inner comment repeats *"the SAME cell gate at production scale"* (`:7271-7274`), but the body calls `_run_cell_gate(cell_key)` (`:7277`) → `_build_cell` at the toy grokking scale (p=97, baked d=128, `test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:551,564`). There is no d=2048 rebuild anywhere in the hook. The audit flags this as exactly the SG11 shape — the validator's *claimed* scale and *actual* scale disagree — so a winner that is fp64-correct at d=128 but breaks at d=2048 (occupancy spill, tile-count-dependent reduction) is accepted and published (`test_coverage_gap_audit.json` RG4).

- **The SG2 mirrored-oracle (real-rank de-mirror + voting fidelity probe).** SG2's B1 anchor is `sg2_kernel_mirror.oracle_step`, which re-implements the *kernel's low-rank* CSA lightning-indexer (drops `idx_UQ`, normalizes `/sqrt(rank)`) rather than the *canonical full-rank* path (`(x@idx_DQ)@idx_UQ`, `/sqrt(d)`) — so `kernel == oracle` by construction for the indexer top-k and B1 cannot distinguish a correct low-rank indexer from a buggy one (`oracle_trust_audit.json` finding 1). The required fix is to **de-mirror** the reference back to the canonical full-rank indexer, and to make the only divergence-detecting instrument — the **N>64 CSA fidelity probe** — *vote* in the verdict. Today that probe only `print`s under `if verbose` and sets no `_ok` flag (`_sg2_l3tc_gate.py:320-333`), and the gate verdict is `ok = b1_ok and aaa_ok and tie_ok` (`:335`) — so an indexer regression consistent with the low-rank mirror passes silently. The same toothlessness afflicts the SG2 tie-probe, which validates the *oracle's own* strategy-A perm builder (a property of the test helper) rather than the kernel's segmented sort (`:290-318`; `test_coverage_gap_audit.json` RG16).

- **The `_emitted_sources` keying bug (polyhedral fake-green).** `build_jit`'s final source-swap checked *only* `origin == ORIGIN_SYNTH`, so a polyhedral/CUTLASS/CK winner left `final_sources = sources` (the un-optimized **template**) yet reported `origin=polyhedral` at the *winning* timing — a fake-green where the published artifact is not the thing that was timed. The fix generalizes the swap to any `origin in _VALIDATION_REQUIRED_ORIGINS` with a stashed `spec._emitted_sources[ckey:origin]` (`COMPILE_AUDIT.md:35-41`; the keyed stash is at `compile.py:6812,14645,8538`). The companion `_VALIDATION_REQUIRED_ORIGINS × {ok,deterministic}` winner gate is otherwise real and fail-closed (`COMPILE_AUDIT.md:15,165`).

- **The IL=4 / atomicAdd determinism trap** (the origin of the autotune fp64-hook): the fp32 self-consistency oracle the sweep uses for timing cannot catch a non-deterministic reduction order, so a `non_deterministic` config that merely clears `np.allclose` could win unless `strict_numerics` was on. The fix rejects `numerical_status=="non_deterministic"` unconditionally by default (`COMPILE_AUDIT.md:43-47`; `compile.py:6873,19195,23667`), and the fp64 `_default_correctness_hook` was added so the tuner re-checks winners against the *out-of-band* hardware gate that originally caught it.

The systematic prevention rules distilled from these incidents (`oracle_trust_audit.json` notes; `test_coverage_gap_audit.json` notes) are the project's standing oracle-trust doctrine: (1) **anchor direction** — every oracle's expected value derives from the canonical *algorithm* source, never from a restatement of what the kernel does; (2) **no two same-file twins** — an fp64 "oracle" and fp32 "mirror" differing only in precision/reduction shape fall to a single co-edit; (3) **operand-discrimination** — for any cosine/dot/selection, include a closed-form case where the correct and plausible-wrong operands give *different* answers and assert both equality-to-right and inequality-to-wrong; (4) **liveness = CI-collected and non-vacuous** — a discriminating instrument behind a CLI flag is not a guard; (5) **no silent reports** — any probe that surfaces a known divergence must set an `_ok` flag that votes in the boolean verdict.

### The recurring full-codebase audit discipline

The hazard catalogue is kept current by a *process*, not a one-off. The owner directive (`CODEBASE_AUDIT.md:3-6`) is: **after every landed step, run a comprehensive line-by-line analysis of the entire codebase** — modeled on the compile.py audit but tree-wide — hunting (1) bugs, (2) dead code to clean, (3) dead files to clean. name: ncu-blocked-runpod
description: ncu/CUPTI hardware perf counters are blocked in this RunPod 8xH100 container and cannot be enabled from inside; needs a pod relaunch with CAP_SYS_ADMIN
metadata:
  type: reference
---

On the RunPod 8×H100 pod used for SuperGrok2 work: `ncu` returns `ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM`. **Unfixable from
inside the container** — `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`/`CAP_PERFMON`/`CAP_SYS_PTRACE` are NOT in the container's
capability bounding set, and `/sys/module/nvidia/parameters/NVreg_RestrictProfilingToAdminUsers` is not
exposed. nsys CUPTI *tracing* DOES work (no counters).

**To enable (user action, host/launch level):** relaunch the pod with `--cap-add=SYS_ADMIN` (ideally
also SYS_PTRACE, PERFMON) or privileged — on RunPod usually a custom template / support request; OR if
they control the host, set `NVreg_RestrictProfilingToAdminUsers=0` in /etc/modprobe.d + reload the
nvidia module. Verify: `ncu --metrics sm__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_elapsed python -c "..."`.

**Counter-free fallbacks** when blocked: nsys timeline (one-launch-per-step fusion proof), cuobjdump
-sass / nvdisasm / ptxas -v (HGMMA/TMA/regs/smem/spills, static), CUDA-event wall-clock → throughput +
analytical-FLOP roofline, cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor. Blocks only: measured
occupancy, warp-stall breakdown, L2 hit-rate, issue-slot/WGMMA-pipe util, ncu achieved-FLOP/s.
See [[supergrok-working-prefs]].

phase0b digests: 0/11
--- align caching with codebase mechanism: peek .fast_build_env.sh ---
# Fast-iteration build env for the SuperGrok1.5 perf ratchet: caching + auto-threaded nvcc + ninja.
# Source this BEFORE any build/gate/roofline_bench/compile command:   source .fast_build_env.sh
#
# WHAT IT FIXES (each verified 2026-06-16):
#  1. DEVICE-COMPILE CACHE — the expensive cu->cubin (~200s/TU). torch called nvcc DIRECTLY, so
#     sccache never saw it (0 requests). We route nvcc through sccache via torch's PYTORCH_NVCC
#     hook (cpp_extension.py L2308 — used by BOTH the JIT bench path and the AOT _ops build).
#     The wrapper .build_tools/nvcc-cached execs `sccache nvcc` => CUDA-native cache (verified
#     100% hit on a recompiled config, "Cache hits (CUDA)").
#  2. HOST-COMPILE CACHE — the C++ bindings/stubs. CXX="ccache g++"; torch's COLLECT_GCC probe
#     (L322) sees through the wrapper so its ABI check still passes.
#  3. AUTO-THREADED nvcc — the wrapper adds `--threads 0`, so nvcc auto-detects the machine's
#     CPU count (parallel gencode/compile phases). Replaces the old FIXED, IGNORED NVCC_THREADS=8
#     (torch 2.4.1 never forwarded NVCC_THREADS).
#  4. NINJA + MAX_JOBS — torch uses ninja by default; MAX_JOBS=$(nproc) parallelizes TUs.
#  Together (1)+(2) = the FULL compile is cached (device + host), not part of it.
#
# The gendeps unblock is still required: torch's --generate-dependencies-with-compile makes the
# nvcc command non-cacheable for sccache; TORCH_EXTENSION_SKIP_NVCC_GEN_DEPENDENCIES=1 strips it.
# Cache-hit CORRECTNESS is unaffected: caches hash the PREPROCESSED source, so any header/macro
# change forces a real recompile (a stale hit is impossible).
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-$0}")" && pwd)"
export PATH="/workspace/.local/bin:$PATH"                 # sccache lives here
# FIX (2026-06-17): torch's check_compiler_ok_for_platform (cpp_extension.py L320) runs
# `<basename CXX> -v`, i.e. the BARE name `g++-cached`, NOT the full $CXX path. The wrapper is
# at $ROOT/.build_tools/g++-cached which is on no PATH dir, so the autotuner's --jit-only build
# died at the ABI probe ("g++-cached: command not found") for EVERY cell. (The bench/load() path
# tolerated the full path, which is why the re-profile built fine.) Symlink the wrapper into the
# PATH dir so the basename resolves too — keeps full nvcc+ccache caching intact.
mkdir -p /workspace/.local/bin 2>/dev/null
ln -sf "$ROOT/.build_tools/g++-cached" /workspace/.local/bin/g++-cached 2>/dev/null || true
export TORCH_EXTENSION_SKIP_NVCC_GEN_DEPENDENCIES=1        # unblock: strip the gendeps flag
export PYTORCH_NVCC="$ROOT/.build_tools/nvcc-cached"       # nvcc -> sccache + --threads 0 (device)
export CXX="$ROOT/.build_tools/g++-cached"                 # g++ -> ccache (host stubs); single-token path for torch's which()
export SCCACHE_DIR="$ROOT/.build_cache/sccache"   # PERSISTENT (was /dev/shm ramdisk -> wiped on instance close). Volume-backed so fast-recompile survives across sessions.
export SCCACHE_CACHE_SIZE=20G
export CCACHE_DIR="$ROOT/.build_cache/ccache"     # PERSISTENT (volume-backed, survives instance close)
export CCACHE_MAXSIZE=10G
export CCACHE_SLOPPINESS=time_macros,include_file_mtime,include_file_ctime
export TMPDIR=/dev/shm/tmp                                 # nvcc cicc/ptxas scratch on ramdisk
export MAX_JOBS="$(nproc)"                                 # ninja TU parallelism (auto-detect)
unset NVCC_THREADS 2>/dev/null || true                    # superseded by --threads 0 in the wrapper
mkdir -p /dev/shm/tmp "$ROOT/.build_cache/sccache" "$ROOT/.build_cache/ccache" 2>/dev/null
command -v sccache >/dev/null 2>&1 && sccache --start-server >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
echo "[fast-build-env] caching ON: nvcc->sccache(CUDA) + g++->ccache | nvcc --threads 0 (auto=$(nproc)) | MAX_JOBS=$(nproc) | ninja"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Time a PREBUILT d=2048 decoder bench .so (task11 A/B/C) — no recompile.
Usage: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=i python time_prebuilt.py <so_path> <label> [batch] [reps] [iters]"""
import importlib.util, os, sys, json, statistics, time, torch
sys.path.insert(0,"/workspace/SuperGrok1.5")
def load(p):
    name=os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(p))[0]
    spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name,p); m=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m); return m
def main():
    p,label=sys.argv[1],sys.argv[2]
    batch=int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv)>3 else 4096
    reps=int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv)>4 else 7
    iters=int(sys.argv[5]) if len(sys.argv)>5 else 20
    rec={"label":label,"so":p,"batch":batch}
    try:
        m=load(p); dev=torch.device("cuda")
        d,total,vocab,seq,layers=int(m.D),int(m.TOTAL),int(m.VOCAB),int(m.SEQ),int(m.LAYERS)
        import tuning.decoder_bench as DB
        flops=DB._decoder_gemm_flops_per_step(d,batch,layers,seq,vocab)
        g=torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(42)
        params=(torch.randn(total,generator=g,device=dev)*0.02).contiguous()
        tokens=torch.randint(0,vocab,(batch,seq),generator=g,device=dev).to(torch.int32).contiguous()
        targets=torch.randint(0,vocab,(batch,),generator=g,device=dev).to(torch.int32).contiguous()
        state=torch.zeros(3*total,dtype=torch.float32,device=dev)
        lr,b1,b2,eps,wd=1e-3,0.9,0.98,1e-8,0.0; bc1,bc2=1-b1,1-b2
        call=lambda: m.tc_train_step(params,tokens,targets,state,lr,b1,b2,eps,wd,bc1,bc2,1,0)
        for _ in range(10): call()
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        walls=[]
        for _ in range(reps):
            torch.cuda.synchronize(); t0=time.perf_counter()
            for _ in range(iters): call()
            torch.cuda.synchronize(); walls.append((time.perf_counter()-t0)/iters*1e3)
        med=statistics.median(walls); tf=flops/(med/1e3)/1e12
        rec.update(ok=True,d=d,total_params=total,layers=layers,seq=seq,vocab=vocab,
                   gemm_flops_per_step=flops, median_ms=round(med,4), min_ms=round(min(walls),4),
                   achieved_tf_s=round(tf,3), pct_roofline_bf16=round(100*tf/989.0,4),
                   tile_m=int(getattr(m,'TILE_M','-1')), tile_n=int(getattr(m,'TILE_N','-1')),
                   dev=torch.cuda.get_device_name(0))
    except Exception as e:
        import traceback; rec.update(ok=False,err=f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}",tb=traceback.format_exc()[-600:])
    print("PREBUILT "+json.dumps(rec)); sys.stdout.flush()
if __name__=="__main__": main()

content.text:
On the ncu problem — here it is precisely, since you asked again:

**`ncu` reads GPU hardware performance counters, which NVIDIA gates behind `ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM` (driver ≥418.43).** The check passes only if **either** (a) the `nvidia` kernel module was loaded with `NVreg_RestrictProfilingToAdminUsers=0`, **or** (b) the calling process holds the Linux capability **`CAP_SYS_ADMIN`** (or `CAP_PERFMON`). In this pod, **neither holds and I can't create either**: being root (uid 0) is *not* the same as holding the capability, and `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`/`CAP_PERFMON`/`CAP_SYS_PTRACE` are **not in the container's capability bounding set** (verified: `capsh` shows `!cap_sys_admin`). A capability absent from the bounding set **cannot be acquired by any in-container command** — and the host's module-param file isn't exposed to the container, so I can't flip that either. → **Only fixable by relaunching the pod** with `--cap-add=SYS_ADMIN` (RunPod: custom template / privileged), or, if you control the host, `NVreg_RestrictProfilingToAdminUsers=0` in `/etc/modprobe.d` + module reload.

On the **33 failed read agents** — you're right, they failed on the **API rate limit** (running two 16-wide workflows at once exceeded the org's requests/min). I'll get full coverage by re-running exactly the failed areas in **bundled batches** (fewer concurrent agents → under the limit). Let me keep the GPUs busy (no Claude cost) and prep the gap-fill while the current workflow finishes.

content.text: The workflow completed: **36 digests succeeded, 33 failed on the API rate limit** (the limit is aggressive — even one 16-wide workflow eventually overwhelmed it as retries compounded). I have the exact 33 failed areas. The robust fix: re-run them in **one workflow with ~8 bundled agents** (each covering ~4 areas, so only ~8 concurrent — comfortably under the limit), iterating if any still fail. Let me build that gap-fill from the known assignments.

  name: 'phase0c-gapfill',
  description: 'Re-run the 33 rate-limit-failed read areas, bundled into 8 agents (low concurrency to stay under the API rate limit)',
  phases: [{ title: 'GapFill', detail: '8 bundled agents, each reads several areas IN FULL, writes per-area digests' }],
}
const OUT = '/workspace/phase0c'
const SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object', additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['bundle','files_fully_read','top_findings','bugs','dead_code','digest_paths'],
  properties: {
    bundle: { type: 'string' },
    files_fully_read: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    top_findings: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'Up to 12 concrete facts WITH file:line across all areas in the bundle.' },
    bugs: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    dead_code: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'NEVER flag gfx942/tpu_v6e as dead (preserved by design).' },
    digest_paths: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
}
const COMMON = `Repo root: /workspace/SuperGrok1.5. You are a Phase-0c GAP-FILL reader re-running areas that previously failed on a rate limit. READ EVERY ASSIGNED FILE COMPLETELY — every line, paging through truncation via offset/limit until EOF. Do NOT grep-skim. Cite file:line. CPU-ONLY (static tools only; never launch GPU). PROJECT TRUTH: production path = L3-TC persistent wgmma megakernel ONLY (fused_<model>_megakernel_tc<Opt>); upgraded = baked levers (decoder FWD_PIPE=1/FWD_STAGES=4 +1.49x, DW_STAGE=1 +2.05x; ViT P1_SUBTILE_S=8 +4.02x). HARD gate=fp64(1e-4;SAM 2.5e-2)+A/A/A. gfx942/tpu_v6e are PRESERVED (never call dead). For EACH area in your bundle, write a SEPARATE digest ${OUT}/<area>.md, then return the combined compact summary (digest_paths lists all files you wrote).`

const B = (bundle, areas) => ({ bundle, areas })
const bundles = [
  B('kernels-core', [
    ['cs_dec_misc','READ IN FULL: csrc/fused/sm_90/{dec_weights.cuh, decoder_layout.cuh, pp_stage_decoder_tc.cuh, tp_layer.cuh, tp_transport.cuh, parallel_config.cuh, sharded_optimizer_kernel.cuh, decoder_tc_selftest.cu}. The decoder flat-param layout (kDecOffsets/kDecSizes), the ascending-CTA determinism mechanism, the TP/PP scaffolding.'],
    ['cs_cells','READ IN FULL: csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_{decoder,vit,mamba}_real_adamw_tc.cu + the 3 *_launcher.cu. The host seam, opt_id switch, no-silent-fallback default arm, SG2 dedicated launcher, -DSG_TUNED_GEMM_IMPL=1.'],
    ['cs_inc','READ IN FULL: csrc/fused/fused_wired_cells.inc, csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_dispatch_table.inc, csrc/fused/gfx942/fused_dispatch_table.inc, csrc/fused/COMPONENT_CONTRACT.md, csrc/fused/megakernel_common_hip.hip.hpp.'],
  ]),
  B('substrate', [
    ['cs_pipe','READ IN FULL: csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/{primitives.cuh, tile_pipeline.cuh, warp_specialize.cuh, wgmma_selftest.cu}. The cp.async ring, setmaxnreg producer/consumer (PROD_REGS=40/CONS_REGS=232), L2PersistScope, DSMEM cluster reduce.'],
    ['cs_common','READ IN FULL: csrc/fused/megakernel_common.cuh, csrc/common/{platform.h,types.h,utils.cuh}, csrc/scan/affine2x2.h. The GridBarrier (sense-reversing, sync_reset), TaskQueue work-steal, %smid pin, PersistentContext.'],
  ]),

    ['cs_opt_comp','READ IN FULL: csrc/fused/sm_90/{opt_components.cuh, opt_stages_precompute.cuh}. apply_optimizer<Opt> single-source ladder; FusedScalars/apply_scalars; muon NS combine; SG11 cosine-gate finalize; prodigy d-update; the grokadamw re-inline.'],
    ['cs_sg2','READ IN FULL: csrc/fused/sm_90/{opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh, sg2_meta_tail.cu}. SG2 CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU meta-net + segmented sort (STAGE -1) + the 26-pointer weight bundle.'],
    ['cs_algos','READ IN FULL ALL csrc/algorithms/*.h (adamw,lion,grokfast,grokadamw,looksam,prodigy,neuralgrok,muon,supergrok11,supergrok15,supergrok2,supergrok2_bilevel_adjoint) + SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md. The canonical per-element math (single source).'],
  ]),
  B('opt-py+bindings', [

  ]),
  B('tests', [
    ['t_gate','READ IN FULL: tests/hw/{test_l3tc_tail_gate.py (1512), sg2_kernel_mirror.py (1002)}. run_cell_gate, _build_cell, _CELLS, the fp64+A/A/A gate, the SG11 warmup gate, why SG2 factory is None.'],
    ['t_oracles','READ IN FULL: tests/hw/{mamba3_oracle.py, test_reference_parity.py, test_multistep_parity.py, mamba_oracle.py}. The fp64 reference (ref_<opt>_step) per optimizer.'],
    ['t_tc','READ IN FULL: tests/hw/{test_decoder_tc.py, test_vit_tc.py, test_mamba_tc.py, decoder_oracle.py, vit_oracle.py, decoder_kernel_mirror.py, vit_kernel_mirror.py, mamba_kernel_mirror.py}.'],
    ['t_rest','READ IN FULL the REMAINING tests/hw/*.py + *.cu not above (megakernel tests, parallel/distributed/zero3/tp/pp tests, wgmma substrate test, l3tc gate helper _sg2_l3tc_gate.py, probes, *_binding.cu). Glob tests/hw and read each.'],
    ['t_nonhw','READ IN FULL: tests/*.py (test_shard_map, test_pipeline_schedule, test_zero3_plan) + tests/tpu/* + tests/conftest.py.'],

  B('harness+profile', [
    ['root_race','READ grokking_race_v2.py IN FULL (2505). make_data_for_task, evaluate, EarlyStopper, _progressive_eval_freq, the matrix (MODE=D), model sizes (race+flagship), _try_fused_train_step (hard-raises on non-L3-TC), dead code (in-file MambaModel).'],
    ['root_build','READ IN FULL: setup.py (1029), wiring_check.py, bench_backends.py, build.sh, .fast_build_env.sh, compile_config.toml, pyproject.toml. The source-set resolution, TunedBuildExtension, the cached-build env.'],
    ['go_profile','READ IN FULL: grokking_optimizers/{profile,profile_maximal,utilization,verify_all,_tuned_inject}.py. What each measures; the SASS audit in profile_maximal (~line 285); the _tuned_inject MACROS table + nested schema.'],
    ['perf_dir','READ IN FULL every .md and .json under .perf/ (oracle_trust_audit, test_coverage_gap_audit, phase1_status_audit, author_queue reports, batch/*.txt reprofile). The perf reality + roofline numbers + open coverage gaps.'],
  ]),
  B('docs', [
    ['doc_hwval','READ HARDWARE_VALIDATION.md IN FULL (1876). The 99-cell on-silicon checklist + sm_90 status (what is 🟡 vs ✅).'],
    ['doc_plan1','READ IN FULL: PLANNING_INPUT.md, OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md, COMPILE_AUDIT.md, AUTOTUNE_LINKAGE.md, PERF_ANALYSIS.md, .roofline_max_playbook.md.'],
    ['doc_plan2','READ IN FULL: .campaign_plan.md, PHASE1_CAMPAIGN.md, BUILD_AND_VALIDATE.md, DESIGN-TC-PIPELINE.md, MAMBA3_REFERENCE.md, SUPEROPTIMIZER_SCOPING.md, SUPEROPTIMIZER_L2_PLAN.md, INTEGRATION-*.md, HANDOFF.md.'],
    ['doc_arch','READ IN FULL all archived_reports/*.md (PHASE3-7, BUILD_REPORT, RESTRUCTURE_PLAN).'],
    ['doc_misc','READ IN FULL: docs/*, examples/** (autotune_demo, toy_tune_project incl the .cu kernels), and remaining root .md (.sam_spec, .sg2_spec, .looksam_lane_plan, .gauntlet_plan, .hillclimb_loop, .morning_report, README.md, ENV_SNAPSHOT.txt).'],
  ]),
  B('tuning+scripts+preserve', [
    ['tune_a','READ IN FULL: tuning/{roofline.py, tune_optimizers.py, decoder_bench.py, vit_bench.py, mamba_bench.py, precision_analysis.py, test_build_injection.py}.'],
    ['tune_b','READ IN FULL the REMAINING tuning/*.py (the _*.py probes/validators). Glob tuning and read each not in tune_a.'],
    ['scripts_all','READ IN FULL: scripts/*.py (check_math_single_source, fast_triage, nvcc_baseline, time_cell, roofline_bench, diag_*) + scripts/*.sh.'],
    ['regpressure','READ IN FULL: .regpressure/** (the *.py parsers, *.sh; summarize the roofline *.json) + .phase2/**.'],
    ['results_chr','CHARACTERIZE results/** + tune11_out/report.json (read .md/.txt fully; summarize the .json key numbers: grok results, ms/step, %roofline).'],
    ['preserve_trees','READ IN FULL (PRESERVE — never flag dead): csrc/backends/hip/gfx942/**, csrc/fused/gfx942/**, csrc/backends/pallas/** + csrc/fused/tpu_v6e/**, grokking_optimizers/kernels/gfx942/{adamw,lion,grokfast,grokadamw,looksam,prodigy,neuralgrok,supergrok11,supergrok15,transformer_decoder,vit,common}_gfx942.hip.hpp. Confirm structure; do NOT flag dead.'],
  ]),
]

phase('GapFill')
const results = await parallel(bundles.map(b => () => {
  const areaList = b.areas.map(([n,instr]) => `### area "${n}" -> ${OUT}/${n}.md:\n${instr}`).join('\n\n')
  return agent(`${COMMON}\n\nYOUR BUNDLE "${b.bundle}" has ${b.areas.length} areas. Read ALL files in ALL areas IN FULL, write one digest per area:\n\n${areaList}`,
    { label: `gapfill:${b.bundle}`, phase: 'GapFill', schema: SCHEMA })
    .then(r => ({ bundle: b.bundle, ...(r || { files_fully_read: [], top_findings: [], bugs: [], dead_code: ['AGENT NULL'], digest_paths: [] }) }))
}))
log(`GapFill complete: ${results.filter(r=>r && r.digest_paths && r.digest_paths.length).length}/${bundles.length} bundles produced digests`)
return results

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Work-stealing GPU pool: keeps all N GPUs busy over a job manifest.
Each manifest line is a shell command; the pool sets CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES per worker
so a GPU grabs the next job the instant it frees up. Re-reads the manifest when it
drains so I can APPEND jobs live (continuous saturation).
Usage: python gpu_pool.py <manifest> [ngpu]"""
import sys, os, subprocess, threading, queue, time, json
MAN = sys.argv[1]; NGPU = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 8
done_file = MAN + ".done"            # set of already-run job lines (dedup across refills)
seen = set()
if os.path.exists(done_file):
    seen = set(l.rstrip("\n") for l in open(done_file))
q = queue.Queue(); lock = threading.Lock(); resf = open(MAN + ".results.jsonl", "a")
def load_new():
    n = 0
    try: lines = [l.rstrip("\n") for l in open(MAN)]
    except FileNotFoundError: lines = []
    for l in lines:
        if not l.strip() or l.startswith("#"): continue
        if l in seen: continue
        seen.add(l); q.put(l); n += 1
    return n
def worker(gpu):
    while True:
        try: job = q.get(timeout=2)
        except queue.Empty:
            with lock:
                if load_new() == 0:
                    if all(not t.is_alive() or t is threading.current_thread() for t in threads):
                        pass
            try: job = q.get(timeout=2)
            except queue.Empty: return
        t0 = time.time()
        env = dict(os.environ, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=str(gpu))
        try:
            p = subprocess.run(job, shell=True, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=1800)
            rc, tail = p.returncode, (p.stdout or "")[-400:]
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            rc, tail = -9, "TIMEOUT"
        dt = round(time.time() - t0, 1)
        with lock:
            open(done_file, "a").write(job + "\n")
            resf.write(json.dumps({"gpu": gpu, "sec": dt, "rc": rc, "job": job, "tail": tail}) + "\n"); resf.flush()
            print(f"[gpu{gpu}] {dt}s rc={rc} :: {job[:90]}", flush=True)
        q.task_done()
load_new()
threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(g,), daemon=True) for g in range(NGPU)]
for t in threads: t.start()
# keep running until manifest stops growing AND queue empty for a sustained window
idle_polls = 0
while True:
    time.sleep(5)
    with lock: added = load_new()
    if q.empty() and added == 0:
        idle_polls += 1
    else:
        idle_polls = 0
    if idle_polls >= 6:   # ~30s with nothing new and queue drained
        break
print("POOL_DRAINED", flush=True)

content.text:
Here's exactly what's in the backlog (87 jobs), with the real numbers — and an important honesty check it surfaced:

## The backlog
| Kind | Count | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| decoder d=2048 timing (prebuilt **A/B/C** × batches 4k–131k) | 27 | the **nvcc-vs-compile-file** 3-point (A=vanilla nvcc, B=compile.py-default, C=compile.py-tuned) + **roofline-vs-batch** curve |
| race-scale per-cell **L3-TC timing** (30 cells = 10 opt × 3 models) | 30 | per-cell latency baseline (Phase 1) |
| **nsys** per-cell fusion+timeline (same 30 cells) | 30 | single-launch fusion proof + per-kernel time per cell |

Real results so far (decoder d=2048, prebuilt, **median ms / TF·s / % of 989 TF·s bf16 roofline**):
```
A_vanilla  B=16384  1971.7 ms  20.09 TF/s  2.03%      C_tuned  B=16384  1919.2 ms  20.64 TF/s  2.09%
A_vanilla  B=32768  3922.9 ms  20.19 TF/s  2.04%      C_tuned  B=32768  3843.5 ms  20.61 TF/s  2.08%
```
Two findings: (1) the roofline % is **flat at ~2.0–2.1% across all batches 4k→82k** → confirms it's **latency/serialization-bound, not batch-limited**; (2) **C (compile.py-tuned) is consistently ~1–2% faster than A (vanilla nvcc)** — the autotuner's real but small win at this scale.

## ⚠️ The honesty check this surfaced
The doc says the **upgraded** decoder is **618 ms / 6.48%** at B=16384 — but these prebuilt `task11` binaries run **~1920 ms / 2.09%** at the same batch. That **3.05× gap is exactly the cumulative upgrade** (`FWD_PIPE=1/STAGES=4` +1.49× × `DW_STAGE=1` +2.05×; the doc literally records "1889→618 ms ≈ 3.05× from session start"). **So the `task11` prebuilt binaries are the PRE-upgrade baseline (~1889 ms), not the upgraded L3-TC kernel.** The upgraded kernel lives in the current baked source (`model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh` defaults).

So part of this backlog is honestly **lower-value** — it's re-timing the *old* kernel at many batches. The right move (and what I'll pivot the queue to) is a **cached build of the upgraded kernel** (fast, reuses `.build_cache`) to measure the real 618ms/6.48% kernel, plus the autotune sweeps for optimizer-max. The nsys fusion proofs + per-cell coverage are still valid. Want me to pivot the queue now to building/measuring the **upgraded** kernel (and start the autotune sweeps), rather than finishing the old-binary batch grid?

content.text:
Good questions — let me clear both up.

## What "optimizer-max" is
It's shorthand for the owner's directive in `SESSION_STATE.md`: **"Optimizers must be MAXED, not just fused."**

The megakernel runs **forward → backward → optimizer-update in one launch** (the optimizer is phase **P3** of the persistent kernel, state resident). The **fusion** is done and proven. But the optimizer **tail kernels themselves are un-autotuned** — i.e., the per-element apply (Adam moment update, Lion sign, Muon Newton-Schulz, the SuperGrok meta-net, etc.) runs at default block size / vec width / register budget, never tuned. The profiler says that P3 tail is **~5.9% of the decoder step** (`618 ms`: P1_fwd 178 + P1_bwd 177 + B1 108 + P2_dW 107 + **P3_opt 38**). "Optimizer-max" = running `compile.py`'s autotuner over each of the **33 (optimizer × model) cells** to find the fastest *correct* config for that tail (fp64 + A/A/A gated).

## Why Phase 2 is the long pole — and it's partly a *scope dial*
Phase 2 has two halves:
1. **Compile-file additions** (S1.4 L2-persistence dim, S1.5 smem carveout, S3.4 negative cache, the verified-bug fixes) — bounded code I draft → apply → gate. **~half a day.** *Not* the long pole.
2. **The optimizer-max autotune** — this is the long part, and it's long because it's a **search**, not an edit: `compile.py` does a Bayesian sweep **per cell**, and each trial is a *real* CUTLASS compile (~50 s–3 min) + an 8-GPU timing + an fp64 correctness re-gate. Hundreds of trials × 33 cells × expensive builds → **~1–2 days** if run exhaustively.

**Here's the honest part you're probably driving at:** the optimizer tail is only **~5.9%** of the step, so *exhaustively* maxing all 33 cells buys at most ~5–6% — **diminishing returns for 1–2 days of GPU time.** It's a dial, not a fixed cost. I'd recommend **bounding it** — cap trials/seconds per cell (e.g. the `--bayesian-trials 50 --max-tune-seconds 900` I'm already using) and prioritize the cells with the most tail headroom — which cuts Phase 2 to **~half a day** while still delivering the owner's "maxed" intent on the cells that matter.

The genuinely bigger perf lever is the **model GEMM phases (~75% of the step)** + the **20% barrier-serialization** — but those are *kernel-architecture* changes the brief fences off as a separate spec (Phase 1 is measure-only; I don't improvise kernel architecture). So within this brief's scope, the optimizer-tail autotune is the main perf work, and bounding it is the efficient call.

Want me to **cap the optimizer-max at ~50 trials/15 min per cell** (half-day, ~95% of the achievable gain) rather than exhaustive? That also frees GPU time for the dataset smoke-runs and the 33-cell verification sweeps. Either way I'll keep all 8 GPUs fed and the ETA refreshed.

content.text:
Checkpoint — substantive progress + one critical finding:

## ✅ Fixed: the autotune build bug (my own pollution)
The autotune failed because my earlier `megakernel_codegen.py --write-all` (Phase 0) left **33 dead per-cell `.cu`** files on disk that `#include` the removed `fused_megakernel.cuh`. The extension build globs `*.cu` → tried to compile them → failed. I removed the 33 untracked dead cells (kept the 8 committed real cells). **Autotune now re-running clean** (past the error, in AOT compile → JIT will saturate the GPUs).

## ✅ All 9 phase drafts landed (`/workspace/phase{2,3,4,5}/`)
Vettable designs grounded in `file:line`: S1.4 L2-persistence + S1.5 smem-carveout dims, S3.4 negative-cache + the 3 verified-bug fixes, the 3 dataset integrations + harness changes, the verify harness, the dead-code removals.

## ⚠️ CRITICAL Phase-3 finding (a real prompt↔codebase contradiction — surfacing, not overriding)
The dataset drafts proved that **the L3-TC kernels are compile-time *size-pinned* to the mod-97 toy config**: decoder `SG_DEC_VOCAB=99`/`SG_DEC_SEQ=4`/single-target (`decoder_layout.cuh`), ViT `49-patch/16-patch/97-class` (`vit_layout.cuh`) — enforced by `static_assert`s + hard `RAISE`s (`dispatch.py:1606/1716`, no silent fallback). Sharp question — and it exposes my actual mistake. Let me answer it straight:

## Why the AOT compile happens — and why it's the wrong thing to be running
**You're right: for *running* and *measuring* we don't need to compile at all.** The existing `_ops.so` (and the `task11`/`tune11_out` binaries) are ready — training and profiling just *use* them. I confirmed earlier that `fused_train_step` runs the megakernel directly on the prebuilt `_ops.so`.

The AOT compile **only** exists inside the **autotuner**, and it's inherent to what autotuning *is*: it searches for a *faster* kernel by building **many different variant binaries** (different macros/flags/register-caps/tile-sizes) and timing each. You can't "tune" by reusing one fixed binary — the existing binary is just *one* config; tuning means generating + testing *new* ones. (Even then it reuses the warm `sccache`/`ccache`, so only the *changed* TU rebuilds — but the **cold first build of the full CUTLASS extension** is the minutes-long, GPU-idle part you've been watching.)

**My mistake:** I made the *compile-heavy autotune* the continuous GPU load. That's backwards. The continuous, GPU-saturating, no-compile work is **training on the existing binary** — the megakernel runs every step with zero build phases. Optimizer-max autotune is a *secondary* perf-tuning pass, not the thing that should be keeping the GPUs warm.

Here's what I think the goal is and how we get there — straight, no hedging:

## The goal
**SuperGrok2 is an optimizer-ranking benchmark at scale.** The question it answers: **which of the 11 grokking-aware optimizers** (AdamW, Lion, Grokfast, GrokAdamW, LookSAM, Prodigy, NeuralGrok, Muon, SuperGrok-1.1/1.5/2) trains **best — lowest validation loss per fixed gradient-step budget, most stably** — across **three ~1.5B-parameter models** (Transformer-Decoder, ViT, Mamba-3) on **real datasets** (FineWeb-Edu, ImageNet-1k, GiftEvalPretrain). MLCommons-AlgoPerf in spirit. Everything else — the fused L3-TC persistent megakernels, the compile-file autotuner, the fp64+A/A/A correctness gates — exists to make that benchmark **fast, correct, and trustworthy** on 8×H100.

## The steps (the critical path)
1. **Scale the models to ~1.5B.** They're mod-97 toys (d=128) today; the flagship configs (decoder d1600/L48, ViT d1664/L48, Mamba d2048/L24) are already defined in the codebase. The L3-TC kernels are **compile-time size-pinned**, so scaling = **regenerate the kernels at the flagship sizes** (layout headers via the codegen + a cached build). *(Caveat I already found: Mamba-3 hits the smem-per-SM cap above ~d=142 — its flagship needs the activation-draining/chunking fix.)*
2. **Wire the real datasets** — single-pass streaming + a **fixed small eval probe** (eval in seconds, not minutes) + the harness changes (cap `evaluate`, plateau `EarlyStopper` for LM/forecasting, keep accuracy for ViT). These pair with the 1.5B models.
3. **Run the benchmark** — train all 11 optimizers × 3 (1.5B) models on the real data at the fixed step budget → the ranking. **This is simultaneously the deliverable *and* the thing that saturates 8×H100** — one 1.5B model fills a GPU, so 8 cells = 8 GPUs at 100%.
4. **Make it production-grade** — the supporting phases: optimizer-max + perf levers (fast), per-function verification (correct/wired), bug-fix + dead-code (clean), final profiling + roofline report vs the Phase-1 baseline.

## The honest connection you've been driving at
**The GPU-saturation problem and the actual goal are the same problem.** I kept failing to keep 8 GPUs busy because I was patching it with toy-scale (d=128) and prebuilt-d=2048 workloads that either can't load an H100 or died in my ad-hoc launchers. The durable answer is **step 1 + 3: build the flagship kernels and run real 1.5B training** — that genuinely saturates the hardware *and* produces the benchmark. content.text:
That lands a much bigger piece, and it reframes everything. Let me say it back so we're locked:

## The bigger picture I was missing
This isn't *a benchmark with some kernels* — it's a **self-adapting, portable training stack**, and the benchmark is just *what we're validating it on*. The real product has two properties I under-weighted:

**1. Portability / "PyTorch-shaped."** Every component — the 3 models, the 11 optimizers, the **compile file**, the **profiling files** — is meant to be **dropped into anyone's project and just fit**, like PyTorch: a high-level Python surface over a CUDA/C++ backend. That's why the compile file has that **portability invariant** I flagged in Phase 2 (config/declaration-driven, *never* SuperGrok-hardcoded — `_DEFAULT_PROJECT_CONFIG`, the `tune_hook` seam, the foreign-project self-test). It's a **general autotuning + megakernel engine**, not a one-project tool.

**2. The megakernel *designs itself to the workload* (the meta-programming).** The kernel + autotuner **co-generate the optimal kernel for whatever it's asked to do**:
- 10M params on 1 GPU → it specializes itself for *that* (tiny tiles, single-CTA, no comm) at max perf.
- **1.5B params with 4D parallelism (DP×TP×PP) + ZeRO-3** → it specializes itself for *that* — the `megakernel_codegen` emits the cell, the compile file tunes it, and the `ParConfig<DP,TP,PP,SP,Z>` template (I read `parallel_config.cuh`) compiles the comm in, with the `SingleGPU` specialization staying byte-identical when degenerate.

So the "flagship regen" I described isn't me hand-coding `d=1600` — it's **the stack self-configuring** for the (scale, parallelism, hardware) point, which is the whole thesis.

## The detail that fixes my GPU confusion: **4D + ZeRO-3 is HOW 8 GPUs get used**
I kept trying to saturate 8 GPUs with 8 *independent* toy trainings. Wrong model. For the real target, **ONE 1.5B model is distributed across all 8 GPUs** via DP×TP×PP + ZeRO-3 (TP/PP shard the model, ZeRO-3 shards optimizer state, DP replicates) — *that's* what fills the hardware, and it's the stack designing itself for the distributed case. The `.parallelism_design.md` I read is exactly this (DP+ZeRO-2 → ZeRO-3 → +PP → +TP, with device-NVSHMEM-TP as the stretch and host-NCCL-TP as the fallback) — and it's currently **DESIGN-ONLY** (the `ParConfig` template, `sharded_optimizer_kernel.cuh`, `ZeRO3Sharder`, `tp_transport.cuh` Loopback/NVSHMEM transports are scaffolded but not wired+validated on 8 GPUs).

## So the refined goal + critical path
**Goal:** a portable, self-configuring, max-performance training stack (Python/CUDA, megakernels that auto-design to any scale+parallelism+arch), **validated** by the 11-optimizer ranking benchmark on three 1.5B models with **4D+ZeRO-3** on 8×H100 — while keeping every component reusable for *any* project.

**Critical path:**
1. **Wire + validate 4D + ZeRO-3** (mostly scaffolded; the 1-GPU-testable pieces first — `ParConfig` instantiation, sharded-opt-vs-fused parity, the cross-rank A/A/A determinism gate — then real 8-GPU) → **this is what saturates the hardware.**
2. **Flagship kernel self-config** (codegen + autotune emit the optimal 1.5B cell per parallel point; decoder/ViT first, Mamba with the smem-drain fix).
3. **Datasets** (real data into the scaled models).
4. **Run the distributed benchmark** → the ranking.
5. Cross-cutting, always: **keep it portable** (no project-specific assumptions baked in) and **make it max-perf** (optimizer-max + the perf levers) + verified + clean.

Do I have the full picture now — the portability + the self-designing megakernel + 4D/ZeRO-3 as the 8-GPU mechanism?

content.text:
This is a **key correction in our favor**: the GPU-side 4D test run shows **14 passed, 1 failed** — so **4D+ZeRO-3 is actually *implemented and mostly working*, not design-only** as the `.parallelism_design.md` contract implied. The DP=2 loopback **ran the real distributed step** (reduce-scatter → sharded-opt → all-gather) via torchrun, and it's **cross-rank bit-identical + A/A/A deterministic**. The build was cached (`ninja: no work to do`).

The one failure is precise and concrete:
```
grokfast/decoder DP=2 vs single-GPU unsharded: maxd=1.53e-04 rel=3.77e-05 (tol 3e-05) → parity=False
```
The distributed (sharded) result differs from single-GPU by **rel 3.77e-05, just over the 3e-05 tol** — exactly the cross-rank fp32-reassociation class the design doc §2.7 flagged (the reduce-scatter sums in a different order than the single-GPU ascending reduction; grokfast's `ema=grad` cold-start nudges it over). So it's either a **fixed-order-reduce bug** (real) or a **tolerance that's too tight for grokfast's extra op** (calibration) — I'll determine which (gated, not guessed).

You're right to question it — **I have not been doing this right**, and your point is the key one. Let me be straight:

**Filling 80 GB by pumping the batch to ~80,000 on the d=2048 *toy* (which has seq=4, 101M params) is unrepresentative nonsense.** Real training memory is dominated by **params + optimizer state + activations**, not a giant batch on a tiny short-sequence model. So a batch that high is a red flag that I was filling memory the wrong way, on the wrong model. The d=2048 toy was a bad stopgap and I over-invested in hacking it.

## 1. Everything else now, specific archs later — understood
I'll complete the **general, portable stack** (compile-file additions + the verified bug-fixes, datasets Layer-A plumbing, the 4D+ZeRO-3 distributed machinery + the in-kernel all-reduce, per-function verification, profiling, cleanup) and **defer the per-model architecture work** (the flagship kernel designs/tuning for each model) until you give me that direction.

## 2. In-megakernel all-reduce instead of a CUDA graph — yes, and you're right it's the faster design
That's exactly the **device-initiated NVSHMEM** path the `.parallelism_design.md` calls the stretch goal. The all-reduce runs **inside** the persistent megakernel, between grid-barrier phases (after `out_proj`, after `ff2`) via device-side NVSHMEM — the kernel **never exits** to do the collective, so it keeps the one-launch fusion and overlaps comm with compute. That beats exiting to host-NCCL even when the host path is graph-captured (a graph kills launch jitter, but it can't put the collective *inside* the fused kernel). The seam is already scaffolded: `tp_transport.cuh` has `NvshmemTransport` (gated behind `-DSG_HAS_NVSHMEM=1`; NVSHMEM isn't installed yet) next to the `LoopbackTransport`. **Caveats I'd hold us to:** it needs a **fixed-order ring reduce** (not naive `nvshmem_sum`) for A/A/A bit-determinism, and NVSHMEM-vs-GridBarrier coexistence + register/occupancy pressure (NVSHMEM can spill → break the 1-CTA/SM occupancy the GridBarrier requires → hang) — so host-NCCL+graph stays the safe fallback while the in-kernel version is the perf target. Net: **yes, do it in-kernel; it's the faster kernel.**

## 3. CUTLASS/CuTe vs hand-rolled vs Python — the honest answer (and the real reason they're slow)
- **No kernel functionality is in Python.** Python is purely orchestration (dispatch, the autotuner, the race driver). All compute is CUDA/PTX.
- **But the persistent megakernel does *not* use CUTLASS/CuTe for its in-kernel GEMMs.** It uses a **hand-rolled `ss`-wgmma (HGMMA) engine** (`wgmma.cuh` — inline-PTX `wgmma` + a `cp.async` ring), because CUTLASS/CuTe collectives are **host-launched and can't run device-side inside the persistent kernel** (it owns its grid and runs fwd→bwd→opt between hand-built grid barriers). CUTLASS+CuTe *is* in the tree (`mma.cuh`, real Sm90 TMA+wgmma) but only on the *separate host-launched* path — and it's explicitly rejected for the persistent megakernel. (`wgmma.cuh` even verifies its descriptors against `cute::make_gmma_desc`, but doesn't run CuTe.)
- **This is the #1 reason the megakernels are slow.** The GEMM phases take ~462 ms vs an ideal ~40 ms (≈11× off) — and that gap is the hand-rolled wgmma running *well below cuBLAS/CUTLASS-class efficiency*, plus ~20% grid-barrier serialization, un-overlapped fp32 epilogues, and 1-CTA/SM occupancy — **not** a physics floor (the roofline at d=2048 is only 6.48%, target 30–50%). The documented fix is to bring **CUTLASS-class technique into the hand-rolled device engine** (multi-stage **TMA** pipeline, swizzle, warp-specialization) — its primitives exist; they're just not yet tuned to CUTLASS level. So when you're ready for the arch work, **upgrading the in-kernel GEMM toward CUTLASS/CuTe-class (device-side) is the biggest single perf lever.**

content.text:
CuTe design workflow is running (5 agents scoping the exact device-side-atom GEMM + the implementation plan to `/workspace/cute_plan/`). On your other points:

## CTA-tiling — it's the central tension, and it's likely the *next* bottleneck after CuTe
CTA-tiling = how the GEMM output is partitioned across thread blocks. Standard CUTLASS tiles the output into threadblock tiles (one CTA per tile), runs **many CTAs concurrently** for occupancy, and on Hopper uses **thread-block clusters** (2–16 CTAs cooperating via DSMEM + TMA multicast) for big tiles.

The persistent megakernel **can't do that** — it's pinned to **1 CTA per SM** because the hand-built GridBarrier needs every CTA co-resident. So ~132 CTAs total, each **grid-striding serially over `kTileM=128`-row output tiles**. That's a fundamentally more constrained CTA-tiling, and it's one of the documented slowness causes (1-CTA/SM = little latency-hiding slack).

So there are **two layers** to CTA-tiling here, and they're why your "implement CuTe → then profile" plan is exactly right:
- **In-CTA tiling** (the per-CTA tile: TMA load → swizzled smem → pipelined wgmma atoms): this is what the **CuTe rewrite fixes** — the immediate win, and it stays inside the 1-CTA/SM model.
- **CTA-level tiling** (occupancy, clusters, the 1-CTA/SM constraint itself): this is **bounded by the persistent-megakernel design**, and after the CuTe rewrite the profiler will very likely show the bottleneck **shift here** — at which point the real arch question surfaces: *is the 1-CTA/SM fusion still the win at scale, or does a cluster-tiled / higher-occupancy design beat it?* That's a genuine arch decision for the post-CuTe profiling.

So: CuTe handles the in-CTA GEMM (now); CTA-level tiling (clusters/occupancy vs the persistent constraint) is the next thing the post-CuTe profile will expose — which is precisely the bottleneck analysis you want.

The CuTe design workflow returned an **excellent, actionable plan** — and the key finding makes this far more tractable than feared:

**The swap is local to one file.** The CuTe atom replacement keeps the exact `sg::sm90::wgs::` ABI in `wgmma.cuh` (`WgmmaAccum<N>`, `make_desc_{A,B}_kmajor`, `wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16`, the fence/commit/wait trio, `wgmma_frag_decode`) — so **no model-stage / megakernel / launcher changes**. And it's an exact mapping: the hand-rolled `SmemDesc{uint64_t}` is bit-for-bit `cute::GmmaDescriptor`, the PTX issue maps to `cute::SM90::GMMA::MMA_64xNx16_F32BF16BF16_SS<Major::K,Major::K>::fma(...)`, ScaleD↔`ScaleOut`. The smem layout *is* `cute::GMMA::Layout_K_INTER_Atom<bf16>`. **TMA is correctly deferred** (CuTe v3.6 builds tensor maps host-side only; the megakernel carves operands at runtime — needs grid-constant `CUtensorMap`s, a later step).

So it's **incremental + parity-first**: (1) descriptor builders → CuTe `GmmaDescriptor` (byte-identical), (2) MMA issue → CuTe atoms (same wgmma instructions), (3) fence/commit/wait → CuTe `warpgroup_*` — all transport-only/parity-clean, then the real perf wins (TMA, swizzle, deeper pipeline) layer on top, NEEDS-PARITY-gated. Let me verify the GPUs took the race and pull up the full plan to start implementing:

content.text:
Great questions — this is exactly the right analysis, and I can give it now from the phase-level numbers (I'll refine it post-CuTe with fresh profiles). Let me also fix my unclear "tension" wording.

## What's hand-built (the inventory)
Everything in the device path is hand-written; the Python is orchestration only. Concretely:
1. **The wgmma GEMM engine** (`wgmma.cuh`) — inline-PTX wgmma, descriptor packing, fragment decode.
2. **The cp.async staging ring** (`tile_pipeline.cuh`, `primitives.cuh`) — manual `cp.async`, mbarriers, the setmaxnreg producer/consumer split. **No TMA.**
3. **The model stages** (`model_stage_*_tc.cuh`) — attention (softmax+causal mask), LayerNorm, exact-erf GELU, the embedding counting-sort, residuals.
4. **The GridBarrier + TaskQueue** (`megakernel_common.cuh`) — sense-reversing grid barrier, atomic work-steal.
5. **The deterministic reductions** (ascending-CTA fp32).
6. **The optimizer math** (`csrc/algorithms/*.h`) and **the Mamba selective scan** — custom algorithms.

## Which of those gains from "standard" (cuBLAS/CUTLASS/CuTe) — quantified
Decoder step @ d=2048 = **618 ms**, and it decomposes as:

| Phase | ms | % | hand-built thing | standard-lib gain? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 fwd GEMMs | 178 | 27.6% | hand wgmma + cp.async | **YES — big** |
| P1 bwd (dX) GEMMs | 177 | 27.3% | hand wgmma + cp.async | **YES — big** |
| B1 grid barrier | 108 | 16.8% | GridBarrier (1-CTA/SM) | indirect (occupancy) |
| P2 dW GEMMs | 107 | 16.5% | hand wgmma, **staging-bound, no TMA** | **YES — biggest (TMA)** |
| P3 optimizer tail | 38 | 5.9% | hand-written apply | small |
| B2 barrier + grad asm | 37 | 5.7% | GridBarrier + reduce | indirect |

The **GEMM phases = 462 ms = 75% of the step**, and their *ideal* tensor-core time is **~40 ms** — so the hand-rolled engine is **~11× off**. **That's the dominant lever, and it's exactly what CuTe fixes** (CUTLASS-class wgmma atoms + **TMA** instead of cp.async — TMA especially helps the dW transposed-strided gather, which the code today calls "out of scope, needs TMA"). Realistic target: 462 → ~120–180 ms.

The optimizer tail (5.9%, hand-written) and the reductions/barriers (custom-for-determinism) are **not** library-replaceable wins — they're either tiny or intentionally hand-built for the fused/deterministic design. The custom optimizers and Mamba scan have no library equivalent.

**Bottom line: ~75% of the time is GEMM running ~11× slow — the CuTe/TMA rewrite is *the* performance story. Everything else hand-built is either not the bottleneck or has no standard replacement.**

## CTA-tiling — straight answer (I was unclear)
**Adding standard CTA-tiling/occupancy would be GOOD for raw GEMM speed, but it fights the fusion.** Here's the clean version:
- CUTLASS gets its GEMM throughput from **many CTAs per SM (high occupancy)** + **clusters** (multiple CTAs cooperating via DSMEM/TMA-multicast). That hides latency and is a big part of why cuBLAS/CUTLASS hit ~90% of peak.
- The megakernel **can't** do that: the GridBarrier requires **1 CTA/SM**, all co-resident. So it has *low* occupancy (little latency hiding) — which is **~20% of the step sitting idle in barriers** + slower GEMMs.
- So **more CTA-tiling = faster GEMMs but breaks "one persistent kernel."** It's a tradeoff, not pure-good — but my honest bet: **at flagship scale (big GEMMs), relaxing the 1-CTA/SM constraint (clusters, or splitting the GEMM-heavy phases out) is net-positive**, because GEMM efficiency dominates over launch-elimination once the GEMMs are large. The CuTe rewrite gets the *in-CTA* GEMM efficient first **without** touching the CTA model; then the profile will show whether the 1-CTA/SM occupancy is the next wall — and if so, **adding CTA-tiling/clusters is the right next arch move.** That's the "good or bad" answer: **good for speed, costs you some fusion, and likely worth it at scale — but measure it post-CuTe.**

## Hand-written vs "maximally-performant standard"
The real comparison is **fusion vs peak-GEMM**:
- A pure cuBLAS/CUTLASS pipeline → ~90% peak *on the GEMMs*, but **separate host-launched kernels** = launch overhead + HBM round-trips between every op, and **no fusion**. Wins at large scale where GEMMs dominate.
- The megakernel → kills launch/round-trips (fusion win) but **sub-optimal in-kernel GEMM + 1-CTA/SM**. Wins at small scale.
- **CuTe atoms are how you get both** — CUTLASS-class GEMM technique (TMA/swizzle/pipelined wgmma) running *device-side inside* the fused kernel. That's why it's the right target rather than just "switch to cuBLAS."

## On the flagship
You're right — the flagship 1.5B build **is** the goal, not a discovery; I'll just build it (codegen parameterized by `(d, layers, vocab, seq)` → flagship layout → 4D+ZeRO-3 across the 8 GPUs). I'll do that alongside the CuTe rewrite.

I'll **continue into the CuTe implementation now** and hand you the refreshed, profiler-backed version of this exact analysis once it's in (so you see precisely where the bottleneck moves). Proceeding.

content.text:
Good — two clean things:

## The mod-97 confusion — fair catch, here's the why
mod-97 is the **current** data (it's literally what `make_data_for_task` generates today). The goal *is* to replace it with the real datasets — but I had the datasets agent keep the mod-97 path **byte-identical and default-on for one transitional reason**: the **kernels are still size-pinned to the mod-97 sizes** (vocab 99 / seq 4 / d 128). Until the flagship resize lands, **mod-97 is the only data that actually fits the compiled kernels**, and keeping it byte-identical means the existing fp64+A/A/A gates and the race keep validating the stack while I'm adding the new dataset plumbing underneath.

So it's a **safety net during the swap, not the end state.** End state: real datasets on the 1.5B flagship models; mod-97 demotes to a fast smoke/gate fixture (or goes away). If you'd rather I just **rip mod-97 out and replace it outright**, I can — I only kept it because it's currently the sole runnable config. My recommendation: keep it as a tiny CI smoke fixture, make the real datasets the actual benchmark. Your call, but it doesn't block anything.

## CuTe atoms — yes, that's the priority, and it's in flight
The `cute` agent is producing the exact-edit spec right now from the detailed `/workspace/cute_plan/` (the seam is local to `wgmma.cuh`, ABI preserved, behind `SG_TUNED_GEMM_ENGINE`, byte-identical OFF — steps 1–3: descriptor→`cute::GmmaDescriptor`, issue→`cute::SM90::GMMA::MMA_64xNx16_F32BF16BF16_SS::fma`, fence/commit/wait→`cute::warpgroup_*`; TMA/swizzle deferred). The **moment its spec lands I apply it to the main tree myself, build the wgmma selftest with `-DSG_TUNED_GEMM_ENGINE=1`, and run the `test_decoder_tc` fp64+A/A/A gate** — and if the agent's CuTe code is shaky (it's finicky), I implement it directly from the plan and iterate against the gate until parity is green. That's the real "do the CuTe atoms" — apply + build + gate, with the GPU doing the verification.

Letting the specs finish; I'll report the moment I start applying the CuTe one, with the build/parity numbers.

7	`make_desc_{A,B}_kmajor`, `wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N,ScaleD,0,0>`, `wgmma_fence/commit_group/
8	wait_group<N>`, `wgmma_frag_decode`) is preserved exactly. **No call site changes anywhere.**
9

12	   populated by the same bit layout the hand path uses (proven bit-identical to
13	   `make_gmma_desc<Major::K>` over `tile_to_shape(Layout_K_INTER_Atom<bf16>, Shape<MN,_16>)`,
14	   see "Determinism proof" below). `SmemDesc` is made a thin alias so `.desc` keeps working.
15	2. issue → `cute::SM90::GMMA::MMA_64xNx16_F32BF16BF16_SS<Major::K,Major::K>::fma(desc_a,
16	   desc_b, c[0]..c[N/2-1], scale_D)` dispatched per N.
17	3. fence/commit/wait → `cute::warpgroup_arrive()` / `cute::warpgroup_commit_batch()` /
18	   `cute::warpgroup_wait<N>()`.
19

24	automatically routes through whichever `wgmma_*` primitives the macro selects, so the gate
25	TU `wgmma_selftest.cu` exercises the CuTe path under `-DSG_TUNED_GEMM_ENGINE=1`.
